title: feat(ui): one Settings window for the per-user settings
body:
Stacked on #4490 - do not merge before #4490.

## What changed

This PR adds one Settings window for the per-user application settings (PR F1 of the UI plan #4245, design on #3025).

- A new in-app window `settings_window.rs` with four sections:
  - **Appearance:** theme and colour vision. A pick queues the same `SelectTheme` / `SelectColorVision` as the Theme door.
  - **Graphics:** line width and anti-aliasing. They use the same `State` setters as before. An anti-aliasing count that the device does not offer stays disabled and says why.
  - **Graphics device (read-only):** the adapter and the backend from the startup GPU line, and the sample counts that the device offers.
  - **Updates:** "Check for updates".
- Each choice applies at once and goes to `prefs.json` or `view.json`. Each section that holds a setting has "Reset to defaults". The file formats do not change.
- The Settings button in the ribbon top band now opens and closes the window. The one-row Settings dropdown is removed.
- The command table of #4490 gets one row: `file.settings`, "Settings…", in the File menu above Quit. It has no ribbon cell, because the top band button is the ribbon entry. `docs/decisions/4493-settings-window.md` gives the reasons.
- The viewport Display menu loses the line width and the anti-aliasing. Its group "Graphics" is now "View options". The grid, the origin axes, the projection, the quality presets and the shading switches stay there as quick viewing toggles.
- The window opening is view state (`State::settings_open`), as the ribbon doors are. No MCP tool and no CLI flag (answer 4 on #3025).

## Screenshots (1366 x 768)

Before: the Settings dropdown.

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/refs/heads/pr-screenshots/4502/before-settings.png)

After: the Settings window, Appearance and Graphics sections.

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/refs/heads/pr-screenshots/4502/after-settings.png)

![after graphics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/refs/heads/pr-screenshots/4502/after-graphics.png)

Before and after: the viewport Display menu.

![before display](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/refs/heads/pr-screenshots/4502/before-display.png)

![after display](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/refs/heads/pr-screenshots/4502/after-display.png)

## Pinning tests

New, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/settings_window.rs`:
- `the_settings_button_opens_and_closes_the_window`
- `the_menu_bar_settings_row_opens_the_window`
- `appearance_picks_apply_at_once_are_kept_and_reset`
- `graphics_reset_restores_the_line_width_and_the_antialiasing`
- `the_graphics_device_section_is_read_only`
- `updates_reset_turns_the_check_on_again`
- `old_prefs_and_view_files_load_with_the_same_values`

New layout test: `layout_window_settings` (`tests/page_layout_windows.rs`).

New unit tests in `settings_window.rs`: `device_of_reads_the_adapter_and_the_backend`, `samples_line_joins_the_counts`.

Updated:
- `layout_window_display_menu` (group "View options", no line width and anti-aliasing rows).
- `the_display_button_opens_and_closes_the_menu_and_the_labels_exist` (the moved rows are not in the Display menu).
- `display_quality.rs`: the line width and anti-aliasing tests now drive the Settings window; `the_graphics_group_offers_...` is renamed `the_settings_graphics_section_offers_the_line_widths_and_the_antialiasing`.
- `update_check.rs`: `settings_toggle_persists_check_for_updates_and_hides_notice_without_dirtying_document` uses the window's Updates section.
- The command table tests of #4490 read the new row from the table.

`#[test]` count of `crates/ui`: 2027 before, 2037 after.

## Gate

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base 3d75878691bd5617778c769d8c695791473a485a`, the head of #4490) and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, on head `6367ef5203641a3f6f6cd7cadcb3f9782ded51ab`: green (19 steps, 0 failed; the `ui suites: lib` step holds the new tests; the site tests step is SKIP on that lane because python, zola and node are missing, and this PR changes no site file); clippy clean. Log: `gate-4493-6367ef5.log`.
- No post, toolpath or project file change, so no example catalog suite applies. No light twin is touched.

## Not exercised

- The real GPU line on a native window: the tests set `gpu_line` by hand. The headless run has no GPU line, and the section then says "Not known".
- The browser build: the Browse row of the theme list is disabled there by the same `browser_files::refusal` as in the Theme door; no test runs the wasm shell.

Changelog: The Settings button and File > Settings… open one Settings window for theme, colour vision, line width, anti-aliasing, the graphics device and update checks. The line width and the anti-aliasing left the viewport Display menu.

Effort: medium

Fixes #4493

title: fix(ui): a gauge length edit never draws the library body over wider steel
body:
Stacked on #4469 - do not merge before #4469.

## What changed

The generic component editor redraws a holder after a gauge length edit. It found the built-in holder by `library_ref`, id or name (`holder_entry`), and drew that holder's outline at the new length. A user holder with a library name and a wider body under the flange envelope then got the library body. That body is thinner than the real steel, and the outline goes into the collision checks.

- New `ComponentGeometry::regauged_holder` (`crates/tools/src/component_geometry_regauge.rs`). It gives the built-in outline at the new gauge length only when both conditions are true:
  - The holder's outline is the built-in holder's outline at the holder's own gauge length.
  - The new outline is the old outline with one straight cylindrical section made longer or shorter. The nose keeps its shape from the nose face, the flange keeps its shape from the gauge line, and the section keeps its old radius.
- Each other case is refused by name, and nothing changes:
  - `NotLibrary`: a library name on another outline.
  - `NoSection`: the outline shows no body section. This is a shrink chuck whose body the flange envelope covers, and also its look-alike with a wider hidden body. The two outlines are the same, so both are refused.
- `component_edit::build` uses the new function. The edit stays one undoable `EditDocumentComponent`.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/4496-generic-editor-gauge.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-ui` lib: `egui_app::tests::tool_library_generic_gauge::a_gauge_edit_never_draws_the_library_body_over_wider_steel` - the look-alike edit is refused by name, it is no undo step, and the outline stays the same. An ER20 chuck copy still takes the edit as one undo step, and undo restores it. This test is red on the parent head `1e899ad` ("a refused edit is no undo step", left 8): log `gate-4496-1e899ad-before.log`.
- `camcraft-tools` lib, `component_geometry::regauge::tests`:
  - `a_look_alike_with_a_wider_hidden_body_is_refused_by_name` - also shows the defect: the library body at the new length is smaller than the Ø50 steel.
  - `a_wider_visible_body_under_a_library_name_is_refused_by_name`
  - `each_library_holder_that_shows_its_body_edits_as_before` - each library entry: a longer gauge length gives the library outline, never smaller than the old outline at any height below the gauge line; a shorter one inside the body section gives it back. Only covered shrink chucks are refused.
  - `a_holder_without_a_port_or_a_body_is_refused`

GATE_RESULTS

## Screenshots

SHOTS

## Not exercised

- A user holder with arcs in its outline. It is refused (`NotLibrary`), because the library outlines have no arcs.
- A covered shrink chuck copy can no longer take a gauge length edit in the generic editor. The user picks the built-in holder again at the new length, or edits the outline. #4455 has the same limit for the holder form.
- No change to toolpaths, posts or the project file format.

UI `#[test]` count: 2010 before, 2011 after. `camcraft-tools`: 286 before, 290 after.

Changelog: The generic component editor refuses a holder gauge length edit by name when the holder's outline does not show the body that the edit makes longer or shorter; it never draws the library body over wider steel.

Effort: high

Fixes #4496

title: fix(post): G43.4 posts write the joint angles of the A/B tilt chain
body:
## What changed

The Fanuc post and the Doosan DNM post wrote the stream's pose letters as the `A` and `B` words under `G43.4`.
The pose law is `axis = Ry(B)·Rx(A)·Z` (`crates/cl/src/cl/pose.rs`).
On the tilt head (`assets/machines/tilthead.mch`), the A rotary carries the B rotary, so the machine reads the words as `Rx(A)·Ry(B)·Z`.
When A and B both turn, that is a different tool axis. The check did not see it.

This PR makes the posted words the joint angles of the machine's own chain:

- `crates/post/src/post/tilt_chain.rs` (new): a prelude function `chainAngles(p)` that every post script sees. It reads the nest of the A rotary (about X) and the B rotary (about Y) from `machine.rotaries` (`parent`, `turnsPart`) and solves the joint angles when A is the outer factor.
- `crates/post/src/machine/tilt_chain.rs` (new): the same rule in Rust, `joint_angles(machine, letters)`.
- `crates/post/src/machine/judge.rs`: `pose_problems` judges the joint angles against the travel, not the letters. The check and the post read the same angles.
- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`, `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: `tilt()` calls `chainAngles` and writes its angles back on the record, so the feed cap and the held angles use them too.

The rule:

- A pose that turns at most one of A and B keeps its letters exactly (the two products are then the same rotation).
- The outer factor is the parent rotary in a head chain, the rotary nearest the work in a table chain, and the table in a table-and-head machine. B outer: the letters. A outer: solved again.
- Away from B = 90 deg there are two solutions. The first one that both travels hold is used, else the principal one (B in -90..90). The travel check then refuses it by name.

Refused by name, in the post and in the check, with the same text:

- A and B both turn and the machine does not state which rotary carries the other.
- A rotary of the A-and-B pair is stated along -X or -Y and turns.
- C turns as well on a chain where A is the outer rotary.

Other posts: I searched every post in `assets/posts/` for the same pass-through. Only `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps` write stream A and B words under RTCP. `mach4.cps` solves its own AC trunnion. `tormach.cps` has a lone A. `linuxcnc`, `richauto`, `sinumerik-810m` and `heidenhain-klartext` refuse tilted moves. Only `tilthead.mch` has two tilting rotaries in `assets/machines/`.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/4417-tilt-chain-joint-angles.md`.

## Changed recorded programs (one by one)

Each change is the old wrong axis replaced by the joint angles. I checked each by hand with `Rx(A)·Ry(B)·Z`.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/multiaxis_deburr_tilthead.nc`: `A16.78 B-47.983` -> `A24.251 B-45.342`, `A16.78 B47.983` -> `A24.251 B45.342`. The lone `A-16.78` of the two other corners becomes `A-24.251` (B stays modal, the same value).
- `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.nc`: the Tilted pocket `A30. B30.` -> `A33.69 B25.659`. The `.camproj` did not change (the rebuild bumped only its version field, from main's format; I did not commit that).
- Test expectations: `vendor_mch_cli` (`A30 B15` -> `A30.867 B12.953`), `program_units` (`A-45 B12.25` -> `A-45.66 B8.629`), `example_catalog` (`catalog_multiaxis_indexed::posts_two_single_axis_indexes_and_one_tilted_pocket` reads the posted joint angles).
- `setup_align_multiaxis`: its hand-built bench machine stated no nest, so the check now refuses its poses. The bench now states "B carries A" (the pose law's own nest). Its programs do not change.

## Pinning tests

`crates/post/tests/tilt_chain_joints.rs` (new):

- `fanuc_posts_the_joint_angles_of_a_chain_where_a_carries_b` and `doosan_dnm_posts_the_joint_angles_of_a_chain_where_a_carries_b`: post poses with A and B not zero on `tilthead.mch`. The forward kinematics of the posted words equals the stream axis within 1e-4. The check's `joint_angles` equals the posted words.
- `a_chain_where_b_carries_a_posts_the_pose_letters`: the same poses on the swapped nest post the letters, and the axes agree.
- `a_chain_with_no_stated_nest_is_refused_by_name`
- `the_machine_check_judges_the_joint_angles_not_the_letters`
- `a_pose_past_ninety_takes_the_second_solution_inside_the_travel`

Red first: with the posts of main (`git checkout 392980120 -- assets/posts/fanuc.cps assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`), the three post tests fail (log `gate-4417-eae2d557a-red.log`).

## Gate (final head c91e47da3, Mac lane, `--pool`)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 852 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes the example catalog suites `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test tilt_chain_joints`: 6 passed.
- Tilt-head users outside the quick plan: `rotary_verify`, `post_not_judged`, `setup_align_multiaxis`, `mcp_multiaxis_deburr_post`, `folder_lists`: all passed.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- Targeted heavy step (P1, safety floor): `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: example_catalog"`: 1 step, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- A table-table A/B chain and a table-and-head A/B machine: the rule covers them, but no shipped machine has one, and no test posts on one.
- `sign_convention: "table_rh"` on a rotary: these posts ignore it, as before. Filed as #4436 (P1).
- The machine model pose (`crates/sim/src/machine_model/pose.rs`) takes explicit joint values. I did not check which caller feeds it stream letters.
- The catalog case `multiaxis/five-axis` (PR #4408) is not on main. It must be rebuilt after this merges.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: Fanuc and Doosan DNM posts write the joint angles of the machine's A/B tilt chain under G43.4 (a tilt head whose A carries B no longer reads a different tool axis); the machine check judges the same angles, and a chain whose nest is not stated is refused by name.

Fixes #4417

body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

This is a sync PR by the rule **Side branch** of `AGENTS.md`. It merges `main` into `side/path-kernel` with `git merge`. There is no rebase and no force-push. The base was `side/path-kernel` at `21fd9e57d`.

## Merges

1. `0af768ad8`: merge of `main` at `39298012074799bf84677c63dc3d34200af8326c`.
2. `a500601ef`: merge of `side/path-kernel` at `500f40256f3fe6e5315084855451eaabebfe1875`. This brings the #4407 fix (PR #4437) and PR #4412. It has no conflict.
3. `d2dfb9dda`: merge of `main` at `6898b02ea3195e9124e6113afd6ab3cee38d0c50`.

Head: `d2dfb9ddab375ff0c0896dd80944659fe9b729d4`. After the gates, `main` moved to `2394b5ad1`. This PR does not include that move.

## Conflicts and resolution

Each conflict is a list where each side added a crate or a step. In each file, both sides are kept.

- `Cargo.toml` (merge 1): the workspace members hold `crates/pathkernel` (side) and `crates/ui-kit` (main, #4394).
- `xtask/src/plan.rs` (merge 1): `BATCH_CRATES`, `ALL_CRATES` and `CLIPPY` hold `pathkernel` and `ui-kit`.

No logic was changed on the two sides.

## Compile fixes

None. After merge 1 and after merge 3, `cargo check --tests` passed for each package one at a time: geometry, pathkernel, motion, sim, post, app, ui, ui-kit and xtask. `cargo test -j 6 -p xtask` is green.

## Re-recorded baselines and readings

- `camcraft-motion` `kernel_laws`: 32 passed.

- `camcraft-app`, release `--ignored`: `offset_pass_start` (`shared_planner`, `kernel_laws_fig8`, `planner_switch`) 9 passed, and `pocket_pass_start` (`kernel_baseline`) 2 passed.

  - `clippy -D warnings`: ok.

title: feat(ui): side panes fold to title chips, kept in saved panel setups
body:
## What changed

Step 1, PR P of the UI plan #4245. A docked pane folds to its title, so that the viewport gets the space.

- The fold flag is the `LeafNode::collapsed` flag of egui_dock. The fold arrow of the dock, the saved panel setups and the new fold law read this one flag.
- A pane in a top-over-bottom stack folds natively to its tab bar.
- A side pane (Browser at the left, Properties at the right) folds to a title chip, 28 points wide. The fold law keeps the open split fraction, holds the split at chip width on each frame, and puts the open fraction back on unfold. A window resize or a drag on the separator does not unfold or widen a folded pane.
- The shell draws the chip in the folded leaf, under its tab bar. The chip shows the pane title, turned to read from top to bottom. One click on the chip unfolds the pane. The fold arrow of the dock also unfolds it.
- Each chip keeps the safety state as text with a glyph (the #4245 E2 rule). The Browser chip shows the counts of blocked, stale and not generated operations, or "Up to date". The Properties chip shows the state of the open operation: "Up to date", "Needs regenerate", "Not generated" or "Blocked" (the reason is in the tooltip). The glyph is a check mark or a warning sign, so the state does not depend on colour. The sources are `status_of`, `stale_reason` and `tool_problem_of`, as in the tree and the operation page. Only a folded pane reads them.
- The chip hover is a 2 px accent frame and a full-ink title. The tooltip follows the pointer.
- Before this change, the fold arrow on a side pane did nothing. It now folds the pane. The viewport never folds: the fold law clears its flag. The viewport arrow stays visible and does nothing, because egui_dock 0.21.1 cannot hide the arrow on one leaf. The decision file records this, and the snap-back of a separator drag on a folded pane.
- A saved panel setup keeps the folds and the open width of each folded side pane. It also writes the mark `camcraft_pane_folds`. A setup without the mark is from an older build and loads with all panes unfolded.
- View > Reset layout and a setup load clear the stored widths. Reset gives the default layout with no pane folded.
- The `show` path of the View door now also corrects the fold counts of the parent splits.

Files:
- `crates/ui-kit/src/fold.rs` (new): the chip widget, the chip rect and the split fraction arithmetic. It holds no dock and no shell state.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/layout/fold_state.rs` (new): the state line of each chip.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/layout/fold.rs` (new): the fold law over the dock, the count fix-up (egui_dock keeps its own fix-up private), the chips, and the setup helpers.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/layout/setups.rs`: the fold mark and the open widths in a saved setup.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs`: two small calls around `DockArea` (the fold law before, the chips after).
- `crates/ui/src/state.rs`: one field, `pane_folds`.
- `docs/decisions/4483-pane-fold.md`: the decisions.

No change to toolpaths, posts or the project file format. Layout is view state: no command and no history entry.

## Pinning tests

`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/pane_fold.rs` (new, in the `camcraft-ui` lib tests):
- `the_browser_folds_to_a_chip_and_its_chip_unfolds_it` (the real fold arrow and the chip button)
- `the_properties_pane_folds_at_the_right_and_the_arrow_unfolds_it`
- `a_stacked_pane_folds_natively_to_its_tab_bar`
- `a_separator_drag_does_not_unfold_a_folded_pane`
- `a_window_resize_keeps_the_fold_at_chip_width`
- `the_viewport_never_folds`
- `reset_layout_unfolds_every_pane`
- `a_saved_setup_keeps_its_folds_and_their_open_width`
- `an_older_setup_loads_with_every_pane_unfolded`
- `a_stale_operation_shows_on_the_folded_browser_chip`
- `the_folded_properties_chip_names_the_operation_state`
- `a_fold_does_not_move_the_camera`

Layout test: `page_layout::layout_shell_folded` (1366 x 768, both side panes folded).

Kit tests in `camcraft_ui_kit::fold::tests` (7 tests: the fraction arithmetic, the chip rect, a click on the chip, the hover step in the dark and the light theme with `contrast::ratio`, and the glyph of the state line).

`crates/ui` `#[test]` count: 2019 before, 2032 after. No snapshot PNG changes.

## Gate

All on the final head `ff940f580`, one lanes run (winbuild, Windows; log `gate-4483-ff940f580.log`, first line `head ff940f580226ff12cfb19063d09c7cf20c2a0444`):
- `cargo check -p camcraft-ui-kit -p camcraft-ui --tests`: pass.
- `cargo xtask gate test pane_fold --crate camcraft-ui`: 1 step, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 20 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (`ui-kit suites: lib` ok, `ui suites: lib` ok, all 16 `ui suites` binaries ok). The `site tests` step is SKIPPED on that lane (python, zola and node are not installed). That is not a pass. The diff does not change the site.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui-kit -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

An earlier head (`485c9d934`) failed three `pane_fold` tests with `Harness::run exceeded max_steps`: the fold law asked for a repaint on each frame. Head `669c595aa` fixes it. The light lane and the example catalog suites do not apply: no post and no toolpath changed.

## Screenshots

1366 x 768, the seeded shell, Contour1 open in Properties.

Before (all panes open):

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4492/before.png)

After (both side panes folded, the job up to date):

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4492/after.png)

After (folded, Contour1 edited and now stale: the chips say "1 stale" and "Needs regenerate"):

title: feat(setup): part-in-spindle mode and table tool stations on a mill
body:
## What changed

- A mill setup can state part-in-spindle mode. The mill spindle holds the bar in a collet. Lathe tools stand on the table.
- `SetupDef::part_in_spindle` (new module `crates/app/src/part_in_spindle.rs`) holds:
  - the stock's length offset register `H` (for `G43 H255`);
  - the collet stick-out and outer diameter, mm;
  - the table stations. Each station gives one tool its own 1-based work offset, an approach side (`-X` or `+X`) and a spindle direction (`M3` or `M4`).
- Two undoable commands (`crates/app/src/commands/part_in_spindle.rs`):
  - `SetPartInSpindle` states, changes or clears the mode. A change keeps the stations.
  - `SetTableStation::put` / `::remove` puts or removes one station.
  - Each command validates the whole next record. It refuses a bad holding, a work offset out of range, a missing tool, and two tools on one work offset, by name.
  - The mode is refused on a machine that is not a mill. It is not stated over a milling operation. It is not cleared while the setup has an operation.
- MCP tools `set_part_in_spindle` and `set_table_station` run the same commands. `get_job` shows `part_in_spindle` for each setup. Both tools are approval-gated as limit edits in live MCP (`mcp/live.rs`).
- The project file keeps the record as an additive key. The loader refuses a record that the commands would refuse, by name.
- The family door (`family_gate`, and again at the post in `posting_family`): an active mode admits the Turn family and a Drill with no cross holes. It refuses milling kinds and cross holes by name.
- Generation and the spindle law read `part_in_spindle::work_kind`, which is `Lathe` in an active mode. The part turns, so the lathe's laws apply:
  - the axial door refuses an off-centre hole by name;
  - the spindle law refuses a bar whose axis is not world Z through the work offset.
- The collet's rating: an unset `workholding_max_rpm` blocks the post by name. The work-spindle limit of #1031/#1174 now applies to a part-in-spindle mill (`setup_workholding::work_speed`).
- The post: no post section writes the stock's `G43 H`, one work offset for each tool, or the station's spindle word yet. A turning section through a milling post would come out as milling. So the program gate refuses a part-in-spindle setup that has work, by name. A follow-up issue owns the post section.
- Docs: the generated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the guide's MCP tool table list the two tools (the `mcp_doc_drift` contract).

## Cause

This is a new feature (part of #2580). Before this change, `Family::admits` refused all turning work on `Kind::Mill`, and a setup had one work offset only.

## Tests

Pins (new files in existing directory suites, no new test binary):

- `crates/app/tests/machine/part_in_spindle.rs` (suite `machine`):
  - `turning_is_admitted_only_in_part_in_spindle_mode_and_generates_and_cuts_on_the_field`: a plain mill refuses Facing; in the mode, Facing is admitted, generates `Ok`, and the lathe field eye cuts the faced end; an axial Drill is admitted; an off-centre hole is refused at generation by name; a cross drill is refused by name; clearing the mode names the op.
  - `an_axial_drill_off_the_spindle_line_is_refused_by_the_spindle_law`
  - `the_mode_and_stations_are_validated_undoable_commands`: bad holdings, a shared work offset (named), offset 0, a missing tool, replace, remove, undo and redo restore the record exactly.
  - `a_lathe_setup_refuses_the_mode`
  - `the_collets_rpm_is_required_and_enforced_and_the_post_is_refused_by_name`: an unset rating blocks `post_script` by name; a G97 op at 3000 rpm over a 2000 rpm collet is refused; the post-section refusal names the setup.
  - `the_mode_and_stations_round_trip_in_the_project_file`: byte-identical round trip, a corrupt record refused by name, no key without the mode.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp/part_in_spindle.rs` (suite `mcp`): `part_in_spindle_tools_configure_the_mode_and_refuse_milling`.

Pin proof: on unchanged `upstream/main` the pins do not compile (`unresolved import camcraft_app::part_in_spindle`, `unresolved imports camcraft_app::commands::SetPartInSpindle, SetTableStation`).

Mutation checks (each file put back to `upstream/main`, pins run, file restored, pins green again):

| Guard | Pins with the old code |
|---|---|
| `family_gate` door hook | red (2 tests) |
| `posting_family` door hook | red (`the_collets_rpm_...`: the generic family refusal comes first) |
| `job.rs` work kind | red (the off-centre hole generates) |
| `spindle_law::turns` work kind | red (`an_axial_drill_off_the_spindle_line_...`) |
| `setup_workholding` collet as chucked | red (the G97 over the rating passes) |
| `posting.rs` program problems | red (an unset rating does not block) |

Gate results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (code head `160a5b9e2`, merged with `upstream/main` `b6089ea6e`; the last commit after it changes only `docs/decisions/3406-part-in-spindle.md`): 546 steps in 62.3 min. 544 ok, 1 failed, 1 skipped.
  - FAIL `app suites: cadmpeg_import` (`stub::a_hung_program_is_stopped_at_the_time_limit_and_its_folder_removed`, `stub::output_past_the_capture_limit_stops_the_program`). These are time-limit tests of a stub program, run under full gate load. Run alone on the same head: 13 passed, 0 failed. This PR does not touch the import code.
  - SKIP `site tests`: `node` is not installed on this machine. The guide edit is one table row; `mcp_doc_drift` (9 tests) reads it and is green.
  - The `example_catalog*` suites ran in the plan: ok.

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `mcp_doc_drift`, `mcp_workholding`, `lathe_workholding_rpm`: green.

## Goldens moved

None. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changes (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" examples/` is empty). The `example_catalog*` suites ran in the quick gate (results above).

## Not exercised

- No post output for a part-in-spindle setup. The post is refused by name on purpose (follow-up #4486).
- No UI rows on the Setups page; the ribbon still hides the turning kinds on a mill (follow-up #4487). No screenshots: no UI change.
- No heavy step: this is a `P6` PR, and AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a `P2` or lower PR no heavy step.
- Light lane: not run to the end. `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main` started, but its release build stalled for more than 40 minutes on small crates (tokio, serde) behind the shared `sccache`. A release build of another worktree on this machine stalled the same way. The run was stopped. AGENTS.md makes a red or missing light run a note, not a block. The reviewer can run it.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill (a process file) has no row for the two tools. The generated reference and the guide list them.

## Overlaps

- #4288 (laser, draft, `conflicts`) edits `family_gate` in other lines and `Family::admits`. This PR adds four lines at the top of `family_gate`. Different hunks; whichever merges second refreshes. Not stacked: #4288 is a conflicted draft feature.
- #4379 touches `gates.rs` (imports and other functions), `posting.rs`, `project/apply.rs`: different functions.
- #4066 touches `schema.rs` and `project/apply.rs`: different fields and lines.
- #4463, #4302, #4238 touch `mcp/mod.rs`, `mcp/live.rs`, `mcp/tools.rs` registration lists: one added line each.

Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3406#issuecomment-7229589585

Effort: high

Changelog: Setups: a mill setup can hold the part in its spindle with lathe tools on the table (part-in-spindle mode, table tool stations with their own work offsets); turning operations and an on-centre Drill generate and simulate there, milling is refused by name, the collet's max rpm is required, and the post is refused by name until a post section voices the stations (MCP `set_part_in_spindle`, `set_table_station`).

Fixes #3406

title: feat(app): Duplicate copies a tool with its holder and component stack
body:
## What changed

- New undoable command `DuplicateTool` (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_duplicate.rs`). It copies a document tool as a new tool. The copy has the same definition (geometry, cutting data), holder body, stick-out, drawn cutter and component stack. It lands the same `ToolRecords` list that `DeleteTool` snapshots. Only the tool number is new (`ToolRecords::renumbered`).
- The copy gets a free name: `<stem> (2)`, `(3)`, and so on. The stem drops a trailing ` (n)`, so the copy of `EM (2)` is `EM (3)`.
- The copy gets the next free tool number from `tool_reservations::allocate`, the same rule as `AddTool`. The command refuses by name, before anything enters the history: an unknown name, an entity that is not a tool, no free tool number, no free name.
- New MCP tool `duplicate_tool { name }` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tool_duplicate.rs`, one registration line). It returns `{ source, tool, number }`. The generated reference `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the MCP guide table have the new row.
- UI: the tool editor footer in the tool library window enables **Duplicate**. A click queues `CommandKind::DuplicateTool`. The window then opens the copy in the editor. The copy is of the tool as it is applied, not of the unapplied draft (the same rule as Duplicate on a user holder, #4338).

title: feat(tools): convert standalone tools to component stacks in one step, with a preview
body:
## What changed

A new command converts standalone document tools to component stacks in one undo step. The tool library window shows a preview first. An MCP tool has a dry run that returns the same preview.

- `crates/app/src/tool_convert.rs` (new): the plan. For each standalone tool it proposes a stack and gives a verdict:
  - the stack is: the tool's library holder as the built-in holder component, then a collet that fits the holder and the shank (none for a Weldon or shrink-fit holder), then the tool itself as a solid cutting item `user:tool:<name>`;
  - `same`: the stack derives the same tool record and gauge length;
  - `different`: the stack derives other values, and the row lists each difference;
  - `no match`: the row names the reason (no holder, no collet for this shank, a lathe tool, a stack that a `ChangeTool` law refuses).
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool_convert.rs` (new): `ConvertToComponents`. It lands the selected rows in one undo step: the new table rows (built-in copies keep their library link), each stack, and each derived record and body. A `no match` row refuses the whole command by the tool name and the reason. Nothing changes then. `same_rows` selects every `same` row.
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool_assembly.rs`: `ToolUpdate` is `pub(crate)`, so the new command uses the same per-tool update as `SetToolAssembly`.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/convert_tools.rs` (new): `convert_tools_to_components { tools?, dry_run? }`. `dry_run: true` returns the preview rows and changes nothing. Without `tools`, only the `same` rows convert.
- UI: "Convert to components…" in the tool list header opens the preview in place of the list (`tool_library_dialog/convert.rs`, `state_tool_convert.rs`). Each row has a tick, the tool, the proposed stack and the result. Only the `same` rows start ticked. A `no match` row cannot be ticked. "Convert selected" queues one `ConvertToComponents`. "Select every row that converts" also ticks the `different` rows. The preview is computed on open, on Refresh and after a convert, never on a still frame. If the history moves after the preview, "Convert selected" is disabled until Refresh.
- An old library holder has the default stick-out: flute length plus shank length. Then no shank sits in the holder, and the stack resolver refuses it. For such a tool, the cutting item gets one shank diameter more of shank, and the gauge length stays the same. The row is `different` and names the shank length change. The decision file gives the reasons.
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the site MCP guide name the new tool.
- `docs/decisions/4339-convert-to-components.md` records the decisions.

## Pinning tests

title: refactor(sim): move FieldPlay and PlayWorker from app to the simulation crate
body:
Stacked on #4380 (merge #4380 first). This branch starts from the #4380 head `31438caa1`. Until #4380 merges, the diff against `main` also shows the #4380 changes. My own change is the last commit, `9351f22ec`.

#4380 now has two more commits (`15626f333`, `2acc52c3e`, to `2acc52c3e`). They change only post and UI drilling files, and no file of this PR. This branch does not include them yet. It takes `main` after #4380 merges.

## What changed

The playback code moves from `camcraft-app` to `camcraft-sim`. Only the world reads stay in app.

- These files move to `crates/sim/src/` with `git mv`:
  - `stock_play.rs` to `play.rs` (`FieldPlay`).
  - `stock_play_index.rs` to `play_index.rs` (`PlayIndex`, and the new plain inputs `PlayInputs` and `PlayOpPlan`).
  - `stock_play_head.rs` to `play_head.rs`, and `stock_play_cut.rs` to `play_cut.rs`.
  - `stock_play_precalc.rs` to `play_bind.rs`. The name `play_precalc` is already in use in sim.
  - `stock_play_worker.rs`, `stock_play_worker_frame.rs` and `stock_play_worker_precalc.rs` to `play_worker*.rs`.
- The plain-data parts that `FieldPlay` reads also move to sim:
  - `FieldView`, `Packed`, `CutLayer`, `PackedBase`, `DEFAULT_TEXELS`, `build_stock`, `build_target` and `subdivide` go to `camcraft_sim::field_view`.
  - `rotary_pose_tol` and `simulate_rotary_slice` go to `camcraft_sim::stock_sim` (`rotary_slice.rs`).
  - `LathePlan` goes to `camcraft_sim::stock_sim` (`lathe_plan.rs`).
- App re-exports each moved item at its old path. The paths are `stock_play`, `stock_play_worker`, `stock_view`, `stock_sim::rotary` and `stock_sim::lathe`.
- `PlaySeed` is now an app newtype over `PlayInputs`. `PlaySeed::gather` reads the world. It also converts each `Planned` op to a `PlayOpPlan`.
- `FieldPlay::from_seed` and the `PlayWorker::spawn*` functions take `impl Into<PlayInputs>`. Callers that pass a `PlaySeed` do not change.
- `FieldPlay::new` and `FieldPlay::with_budget` read the world. They are now the methods of the app trait `stock_play::FieldPlayWorld`. Three test files import that trait. No assertion changed.
- The worker reads the host clock from `PlayInputs::clock`. App passes `clock::monotonic`, which uses the #31 wasm32 clock seam. camcraft-sim gets no new dependency.
- The Gate maps of the playback suites name the new sim modules. Then a change in `crates/sim/src/play*.rs` selects them in the quick gate.

The picture, the Deviate verdict and the post gate do not change. The cut code is the same code. Only its imports, the seed conversion and the clock reads changed.

- Red before the change: yes. On the unchanged code the pins do not compile: `error[E0432]: unresolved imports super::FieldPlay, super::PlayInputs, super::PlayOpPlan, super::Progress` and `unresolved import crate::play_worker`.

title: feat(sketch)!: quick ops - shapes by dimensions as profiles with a 2D Contour
body:
## What changed

- `camcraft-geometry` gets `sketch_recipe::SketchRecipe`. It has four shapes: rectangle (optional corner radius), circle, obround and regular polygon (across flats or across corners).
- A recipe compiles to exact `Line`, `Arc` and `Circle` primitives in a `SketchData`. The outline is closed, counterclockwise and centred on the profile origin, on the layer `outline`.
- A bad dimension is refused by name and never clamped. The refusals are: not finite, below 0.1 mm, above 100000 mm, a negative corner radius, a corner radius larger than half the smaller side, an obround wider than long, fewer than 3 or more than 1000 sides, and a straight edge shorter than 0.1 mm.
- `Sketch` gets `recipe: Option<SketchRecipe>`. `SketchDto` stores it as `recipe`. `PROJECT_VERSION` goes from 84 to 85.
- On load, the stored recipe is compiled again. If it does not give the stored outline bit for bit, the file is refused by the profile's name.
- New undoable commands: `CreateSketchRecipe`, `EditSketchRecipe` and `AddQuickOp`. `AddQuickOp` is one `BatchCommand`: the recipe profile and a 2D Contour on it. One undo removes the two.
- `EditSketchRecipe` writes the new outline. The operations on the profile go stale through their existing stamp.
- New MCP tools in `crates/app/src/mcp/sketch_recipe_tools.rs`: `add_sketch_recipe`, `edit_sketch_recipe` and `add_quick_op`. `get_job` profiles show `recipe`.
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` is generated again. The guide table names the three tools.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/3194-sketch-recipes.md`.

## Cause

Users who cut simple shapes without a CAD model had no way to state a shape by its dimensions.

## Tests

Pinning tests:

- `camcraft-geometry` `dxf` suite, module `sketch_recipe` (9 tests): each shape is one closed chain with the exact perimeter and bounds; bad dimensions are refused by name; the same recipe gives the same outline bit for bit.
- `camcraft-app` `mcp` suite, module `sketch_recipe` (5 tests):
  - `each_quick_op_shape_generates_verifies_and_posts_with_no_model`: four shapes, generate, `verify` ok, Fanuc post, lowest feed Z is the stated depth, G2/G3 for the round shapes.

  - `a_recipe_profile_round_trips_the_project_file_and_edits_after_load` (v85 written, recipe and placement read back, a changed recipe refused as corrupt).

| Guard | Pin | Without guard | Restored |

| recipe must give the stored outline on load | `a_recipe_profile_round_trips_...` | red | green |

The one red step was `app suites: continuous_4axis_part`: `the_committed_project_uses_the_current_file_version` asks for the new file version. title: feat(mcp): hole patterns from numbers for Drill, Bore and Thread
body:
## What changed

- New module `camcraft_geometry::hole_pattern`. `HolePattern::points()` gives the hole centres of four recipes:
  - a point list;
  - a line (start, pitch, count, angle);
  - a grid (start, X and Y pitch, X and Y count, angle; holes along X first);
  - a bolt-hole circle (centre, diameter, count, start angle), full or partial (`angular_pitch` or `span`).
- The coordinates use plain trigonometry: x = cx + r cos a, y = cy + r sin a (Smid, *CNC Programming Handbook*).
- The module refuses bad numbers by the field name: non-finite values, a count of 0, a pitch or diameter of 0 or less, two holes on the same place, a partial circle that closes on itself, and more than 10,000 holes.
- New MCP tool `add_hole_pattern` (`crates/app/src/mcp/hole_pattern_tools.rs`). It makes a Drill, Bore or Thread operation on the stock, with no 3D model:
  - The holes start at `top`. The default is the stock top of the active setup. With no stock and no `top`, the tool refuses by name.
  - `diameter`, `depth` and `through` set each hole. `params` patches the other fields (cycle, pitch, ...), but not `holes`.
  - Seed heights that measure from the model measure from the stock. A height stated in `params` still wins.
  - `spot {tool, depth, name}` adds a spot-drill Drill operation (`cycle: spot`) on the same holes, ahead of the main operation.
  - The two operations are one undo step (`History::begin_group` / `commit_group`, a `BatchCommand`). Both commands are built and checked before either runs, so a refusal changes nothing.
  - A hole off the stock footprint is made, with a `warning` that names it.
- `edit::kind_index` and `edit::patched` are now `pub(super)`, so that the new tool uses the same seed and patch path as `add_operation`.
- Docs: `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` is regenerated (`camcraft-cli mcp reference`). The MCP guide has a new row for the tool.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3195-hole-patterns.md`.

## Cause

Before this change, an agent had to type each hole as JSON to drill a pattern without a model. A stock-only Drill operation also failed at generate with "Top of Part Z (From: model top, offset 0) is unresolved: no model loaded".

## Tests

Pins (all red on unchanged `upstream/main`, green now):

- `crates/geometry/tests/geo2d/hole_pattern.rs` (joins the `geo2d` suite): six tests. They cover each recipe, Smid's six-hole circle at 30 degrees, a partial circle by pitch and by span, and the named refusals. Red before the fix: `unresolved import camcraft_geometry::hole_pattern`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp/hole_pattern.rs` (joins the `mcp` suite): six tests. Red before the fix: `unknown tool 'add_hole_pattern'`.
  - `a_bolt_circle_with_a_spot_drill_is_one_undo_step_and_posts_g81`: spot and drill ops, hole values, one undo and one redo, generate, verify ok, Fanuc post with `G81` at the four circle points.
  - `a_grid_pecks_with_g83_and_round_trips_the_project_file`: 3 x 2 grid, Auto cycle past 4 x D posts `G83`, then save, open, and the same holes.
  - `a_tapped_line_after_its_tap_drill_posts_g84`: tap drill, then a `TAP-M6` line with the tap cycle, verify ok, post with `G84`.
  - `a_line_and_a_point_list_fill_bore_and_thread_holes`: Bore and Thread holes.
  - `bad_numbers_are_refused_by_name_and_change_nothing`: ten refusals by name with no operation added, and the off-stock warning.
  - `no_stock_and_no_top_is_refused_by_name`.

Mutation checks (each guard removed, the pin run, then the guard restored):

- M1, no stock-height swap: 3 MCP pins red ("no model loaded" at generate).
- M2, no build of the main op again after the spot: the bolt-circle pin is red (the spot posts after the drill).
- M3, no refusal of `holes` in `params`: `bad_numbers...` is red.
- M4, no partial-circle full-turn guard: `degenerate_and_non_finite...` is red.

Gate on the final head `e152c869a`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 1015 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 37.9 min. This includes `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens`, `mcp`, `mcp_doc_drift`, `post suites: script_goldens` and `geometry suites: geo2d`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. The quick gate ran the catalog and golden suites above. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "examples/catalog/**"` is empty. The change adds a tool and touches no generator or post.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes and `cargo xtask gate light` did not run. This is a P6 draft. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" asks for no heavy step on it. The light lane is owed before the PR is flagged ready.
- No UI form. The Stock/Sketch form that the issue names goes to a follow-up issue, which is linked in a comment below. Done means of #3195 lists no UI.
- A Sketch of circles as the pattern source is not in this PR. The follow-up issue covers it with the UI form.
- No screenshots: no UI change.

The new files have no overlap. Registry lines in other open PRs touch the same files, but different functions:
- `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` and `crates/app/src/mcp/mod.rs`: #4302, #4288, #4238, #4438 (module and chain list appends).

title: fix(post): keep Mazak probe labels unique in numbered programs
body:
## Problem and change

With Sequence numbers set to Every block, the Mazak probe macro wrote targets such as `N110 N9001`.
The `GOTO9001` branch had no standalone target. Ordinary sequence numbers could also duplicate probe labels.

The post now records used N numbers in one program-scoped set.
Automatic numbers keep the selected start and increment, and skip used numbers.
Probe labels skip used numbers and are reserved before their numbered branch and alarm blocks.
The existing `rawBlock` function writes each standalone label without an automatic prefix.
The allocator refuses a nonpositive rounded increment or arithmetic that cannot advance to a finite number.

The post engine creates a new script context for each program. The set spans sections within that program only.
Default output with numbering off remains unchanged. Probe motions, alarm conditions and feeds do not change.
No dependency or process file changes.

Effort: high

Base: `NeoTech/Camcraft main 1cf7390dc0acc3248f8e98a6612d6fe6c6001a74`.
Head: `a34a2e5d8273ccf3d3f5582194bee2cab53b88a5`.
Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4342#issuecomment-7229322032

## Reproduction before fix

Windows x64, Rust 1.100.1, four build jobs, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`.
The tests post the existing `recorded/inputs/probe_t7_bore_g55.cnc` stream through `engine::run_with`.
The production implementation stayed unchanged at the exact base above for this reading.

```text
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_probe mazak_sequence_labels:: -- --nocapture
```

At this stage the module held the three original regression tests. All three failed: 0 passed, 3 failed, exit 101.
The cold build took 11 min 39 s. The tests took 0.17 s.

- `every_block_probe_labels_are_unambiguous_jump_targets`: `GOTO9001` had zero standalone `N9001` targets. The actual line was `N110 N9001`.
- `probe_labels_never_collide_with_numbered_blocks`: start 1 and increment 1000 emitted `N9001` more than once.
- `probe_labels_remain_unique_across_sections_and_word_spacing`: the two-section program also duplicated `N9001`.

The three assertions remain unchanged. The final module adds the golden and invalid-option tests below.
To repeat the baseline, copy the final test module and registration into an isolated worktree at the base.
Run each of the three original test names with
`cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_probe mazak_sequence_labels::<name> -- --exact --nocapture`.

## After fix and final-head checks

The five tests in `mazak_sequence_labels` pass. The complete `script_probe` suite passes 44 tests.
The new cases cover all numbering modes, start 1/increment 1000, starts 8999/9000/9001,
the declared maximum start 999999/increment 10000, two sections, and word spacing on and off.
Raw nonadvancing numeric options are refused by name.

Pinning tests in the existing `script_probe` directory suite:

- `mazak_sequence_labels::every_block_probe_labels_are_unambiguous_jump_targets`
- `mazak_sequence_labels::probe_labels_never_collide_with_numbered_blocks`
- `mazak_sequence_labels::probe_labels_remain_unique_across_sections_and_word_spacing`
- `mazak_sequence_labels::nonadvancing_sequence_options_are_refused_by_name`
- `mazak_sequence_labels::every_block_probe_matches_its_golden`

The final-head post checks pass: 1,418 tests across ten targets.

| Target | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| lib | 184 |
| post_engine | 143 |
| script_arcs | 49 |
| script_cycles | 122 |
| script_dialects | 175 |
| script_edm | 87 |
| script_goldens | 440 |
| script_probe | 44 |
| script_rotary | 66 |
| script_wcs | 108 |

The commands were `cargo test -j4 -p camcraft-post --lib`, then
`cargo test -j4 -p camcraft-post --test <target>` for each named integration binary.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes in 1 min 50 s.

Validation uses the touched-binary and strict-clippy alternative in `work-issue` section 3.
The quick dry run selects 42 steps. The ten directly affected post targets ran as above.
The 21 other app suites and two prebuild steps did not run through that full quick plan.

The nine required app example suites pass: 80 tests passed, with four existing heavy tests ignored.
Each ran with `cargo test -j4 -p camcraft-app --test <target>`:

title: fix(post): honor rotary sign conventions in G43.4 output
body:
## Problem and change

Fix #4436 (P1, effort:high). A `table_rh` rotary needs the opposite sign from the tool-relative pose. Fanuc and Doosan DNM wrote `A30.` where the machine needed `A-30.`. The travel check also used the wrong sign on an asymmetric range.

Both G43.4 posts now apply the resolved convention when they write rotary words. The existing resolver uses the axis setting, then the machine setting, then `tool_rh`. The machine pose check uses the same signed angle. Its lone-X path applies the axis direction before the convention.

The default `tool_rh` program stays byte-identical. Modal angle memory, feed calculations, Mach4 and the chain solver do not change. No dependency, file format or process file changes.

Baseline: `e80c70942c9484e22d4dfa2110590473a5e49875`.
Validated head: `3c0dc8eb7406aaaea4ccb752c8989c3e7c94284d`.

## Regression tests

The baseline fails on A30 versus A-30, asymmetric pose travel and the lone-X convention. The `tool_rh` control passes. All six pins pass in the existing `camcraft-post` `script_rotary` suite:

- `rotary_sign::g43_4_posts_use_machine_and_axis_sign_conventions`
- `rotary_sign::g43_4_tool_rh_keeps_the_default_program`
- `rotary_sign::g43_4_travel_check_judges_the_posted_sign`
- `rotary_sign::lone_x_travel_applies_convention_after_the_axis_direction`
- `rotary_sign::tormach_refuses_its_own_word_outside_the_signed_travel`
- `rotary_sign::g43_4_posts_refuse_explicit_c_live_tool_work`

The pins cover both posts, inherited and per-axis settings, initial and modal words, and acceptance and refusal at signed travel limits.

## Verification

An independent agent ran these checks on the validated head, with Windows, Rust 1.100.1 and MSVC:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Focused quick selection | PASS: all 97 executable steps; 1,978 tests passed, 6 expected ignored, zero failures. |
| `script_rotary` | PASS: 72 tests, including all six pins. |
| Post clippy, all targets, warnings denied | PASS. |
| Light lane | PASS: all five executable steps and all 11 twins; zero failures or ignored tests. |
| P1 heavy step, `app heavy: lathe_workholding_kinds` | PASS: `every_slow_kind_on_a_mill_turn_keeps_the_work_spindle_within_the_chuck` ran; one passed, zero failed or ignored, 45.73 seconds. |
| Formatting and whitespace | New test and suite registration PASS; diff check PASS. The judge retains 12 formatter hunks, 76 edit lines, identical to the baseline. No formatting defect was introduced. |

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base e80c70942c9484e22d4dfa2110590473a5e49875 --only 'post suites:' --only 'app suites:'
cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets --locked --offline -j 4 -- -D warnings
cargo xtask gate light --only 'motion light:' --only 'app light:'
cargo xtask gate heavy --base e80c70942c9484e22d4dfa2110590473a5e49875 --only 'app heavy: lathe_workholding_kinds'
```

Process environment: `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_SWEEP=off`, `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`. No `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` override.

The quick selection runs all mapped test steps from the 99-step plan, without two redundant all-target prebuilds. The light selection runs all five test steps from the six-step plan, without its redundant prebuild. Each selected step compiles its own target. The single P1 heavy test posts Rotary Contour within the chuck and refuses unsupported five-axis kinds by name.

These existing app blocking regressions also pass on the final head:

- `control_comp::the_lathe_and_the_other_mill_posts_refuse_a_control_op_by_name_and_the_gate_blocks`
- `per_op_files::a_refusal_in_op_two_writes_nothing`
- `c_axis_live::every_post_without_c_or_without_the_machines_words_refuses_by_name`

Evidence is preserved locally in `source/.claude/tmp/4436-evidence/`: `final-head-quick.log`, `final-head-clippy.log`, `final-head-light.log`, `final-head-heavy.log`, and `verification-summary.md`. These logs are not source changes.

## Scope and review

The Tormach pin checks its existing named refusal before an out-of-travel A20 word. Actual `Move::rotary` C input states `LiveTool = radial`; both G43.4 posts return the named capability warning. The app blocks any counted warning before it returns `Posted`. The engine and standalone post CLI can retain program text with warnings. This unchanged lower-level contract adds no C live-tool support or shared C-check conversion.

PR #4371 was inspected at `ce23fdaa8d18ae3784604f2ad1198316cdf7277d`. Its retract and section-preamble edits do not touch the angle writer or machine judge changed here. No retract work is included. The #4417 branch was inspected at `2ede3d05710529d59bb1e0e88761977de23ea057`; its joint-angle conversion precedes this sign conversion. This PR adds no chain solver.

[Decision record](https://github.com/seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech/blob/3c0dc8eb7406aaaea4ccb752c8989c3e7c94284d/docs/decisions/4436-rotary-sign-convention.md).
[Writer record](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4436#issuecomment-7229039456).

No physical control or machine run was performed. This contributor PR needs the upstream collaborator review required by the repository.

Effort: high
Changelog: Fanuc and Doosan DNM posts honor rotary sign conventions, and machine travel checks use the same signed pose angles.

Fixes #4436

title: feat(simview): camcraft-sim check judges a 3-axis G-code file headless
body:
## What changed

- A new crate `crates/simview` (package `camcraft-simview`) holds the binary `camcraft-sim`. It has no edge to `camcraft-app` or `camcraft-ui`.
- `camcraft-sim cl <file.cl> ...` is the old binary of the sim crate. It moved here with the same arguments, output and exit codes. Its three tests moved with it (`crates/simview/tests/check/cl_cmd.rs`).
- `camcraft-sim check <file.nc> --stock <box> --tools <T map> (--post <.cps> | --dialect <name>) [--machine <.mch>] [--wcs G54=x,y,z]... [--fixture <box>]... [--cell <mm>]` is new. It parses the program with `camcraft-gcode` and runs these checks:
  - post: the machine kind that the post serves, `programUnits`, `workOffsetMax` (manifest only, no hook runs);
  - stock: a rapid through the material that is left, move by move in the field stock;
  - holder law: the shank and holder bands against that material;
  - fixture law: the region-free laws of `verify` over the `--fixture` boxes;
  - machine limits: the #2585 judgment, in program coordinates;
  - machine model: the spindle side against the work side of the generated model of #2584, at `work + --wcs`.
- Exit codes: 0 each check ran and passed; 1 bad input; 2 a check failed (each finding names its NC line); 3 a check was not judged (each is named). 2 wins over 3.
- A/B/C words refuse by name (the parser). An unmapped T refuses. A `.camtools` file refuses by name (follow-up #4465).
- `camcraft-sim` drops its `tracing-subscriber` dependency (only the moved binary used it).
- `xtask` lists `simview` in `BATCH_CRATES`, `ALL_CRATES` and `CLIPPY`, and its fixtures follow.
- `docs/decisions/2574-standalone-camcraft-sim.md` records the #2574 research decisions and the crate edges with their imported items. `docs/decisions/2586-simview-check.md` records the decisions of this slice.

Process change: yes

## Cause

The maintainer asked for a stand-alone `camcraft-sim` (#2574). This is its first code slice.

## Tests

Pins, in `crates/simview/tests/check/` (one directory suite, 13 tests):
- `exits::check_exits_0_when_each_check_ran_and_passed`
- `exits::check_exits_3_and_names_the_missing_machine_file`
- `exits::check_exits_3_and_names_the_missing_work_offset`
- `exits::check_exits_3_when_the_holder_stack_is_not_stated`
- `exits::check_refuses_bad_input_with_exit_1` (missing file, an A word, a lathe machine, bad `--wcs`, bad dialect, no post, a bad box, `.camtools`, an unmapped T, no tools, no file)
- `findings::check_names_the_line_of_a_travel_past_the_stroke`
- `findings::check_names_the_line_of_a_machine_part_collision` (with the holder law finding)
- `findings::check_names_the_line_of_a_rapid_through_material`
- `findings::check_names_the_line_of_a_fixture_hit`
- `catalog::check_runs_on_the_fanuc_catalog_program_for_the_default_vmc`: `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc` with `fanuc.cps` on `3axis-vmc.mch`. Exit 3: that machine file states no stroke and no part tree, and the closing G28 moves have no `--wcs`. Each is named. The stock and holder checks pass on the whole program.
- `cl_cmd::*`: the old behaviour of the moved binary.

Red before the change: yes. `upstream/main` has no `check` subcommand and no `camcraft-simview` package, so each pin fails.

Mutations (each guard disabled, its pin run, then restored; restored suite green, 13 passed):
- not-judged exit code: red
- limit judgment: red
- machine-part collision: red
- rapid through material: red
- unmapped T refusal: red
- holder law: red
- fixture law: red

Gate on the final head (a4ee60c6b), against upstream/main 1cf7390dc: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` fell back to batch (the workspace manifest changed). Result: 1017 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, clippy included (wall 31.4 min).

New top-level test binary: `crates/simview/tests/check/` is the first suite of a new crate. The old binary test moved into it from `crates/sim/tests/sim_timeline/`.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-simview -p camcraft-sim -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
`cargo test -p xtask`: green.

## Goldens moved

None. No post, toolpath, golden or catalog program changes. The catalog program is read, not written. The example catalog suites are not reached.

## Heavy lanes

Not run. This is a `P4` PR. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) gives a heavy step only to a `P1` PR under the safety floor.

## Not exercised

- The window and playback (#2587), the job file (#2588), the button (#2589) and the release packages (#2590) are later slices.
- A `.camtools` library (#4465).
- 4- and 5-axis programs (#2592).
- The machine model uses the generated bodies only. Its frame puts the spindle nose on the table top at joint zero (#2584). A real controller's machine zero is different, so a user gives `--wcs` in that frame.
- G28 and G30 return to machine zero. A machine file that states another home is not read.

## Overlaps

- #4383 and #4258 change the `members` line of the root `Cargo.toml` (a different entry). Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: New `camcraft-sim check`: judges a posted 3-axis G-code file headless against a post, a machine file, the stock, the tools and the fixtures, with exit codes 0/1/2/3 and NC line numbers. The old headless stock simulation is now `camcraft-sim cl`.

Effort: max

Fixes #2586

title: feat(sim): simulate and verify external NC programs against the setup
body:
## What changed

`camcraft_app::nc_sim` simulates an external NC program against the selected setup. Its entry points are `simulate_nc`, `simulate_nc_text`, `unmapped_tools` and `play_seed`. The runner reads the document and changes nothing. It is not an undoable command. The MCP tool and CLI command are follow-up #2220.

The tool map reads an explicit `T -> tool` mapping first, then document tool numbers, then numbered `.camtools` rows. It reports each unmapped number and refuses simulation if any number lacks cutter geometry. Only supported milling cutters pass the map.

The runner transforms program coordinates into world millimetres with `world = origin + sign * program_mm`. It reads the setup WCS or caller origins for `G54`..`G59`. A single negated in-plane axis reverses arc sense. An unstated work offset or turned setup WCS is refused.

The runner cuts the setup stock with the column engine and measures deviation against the target. It checks target gouges, fixture collisions and machine limits. Findings name their 1-based NC line. Machine checks include travel, feed, spindle speed, tool size and changer capacity. `play_seed` builds a `PlaySeed` for `FieldPlay` playback. Missing stock is refused by name.

`camcraft-app` now depends on `camcraft-gcode`. The workspace entry returns because the app uses it. `docs/decisions/2218-nc-sim-runner.md` records this dependency and the review-fix decisions.

## Latest review findings addressed

1. **Initial motion.** The caller must confirm the parser's actual start with `NcSimOptions::initial_position_known`. The runner preserves the complete first move. Unknown starts refuse simulation and playback for straight moves and arcs. It does not collapse a traverse between clear endpoints.
2. **Unsupported taper tips.** The shared tool-resolution guard applies `taper::is_unread_tip` to explicit, document and library sources. It refuses sane flat and ball taper tips instead of checking them as sharp cones.
3. **Mesh fidelity.** One preparation guard checks the selected stock, target and fixtures. Unknown fidelity refuses simulation and playback. Reduced stock or target fidelity tightens the tolerance by the maximum excess. The guard uses the strict law because the checks include shanks and holders. An explicit tolerance cannot restore an exhausted fidelity budget. Known coarse fixture boxes retain their chord growth. Target and fixture overrides replace their corresponding document inputs. Playback receives the same adjusted tolerance.

## Pin proof

The tests join the existing `stock_sim_document` binary. Original integration pins are in `nc_program.rs`; review pins are in `stock_sim_document/nc_safety.rs`. No new test binary was added.

Each of these four mutations caused behavioral failures. Each fix was then restored. The final restored suite passed with **29 tests and 0 failures**.

| Mutation | Failing pins in `nc_program::safety` |
|---|---|
| Restore first-move collapse | `nc_first_rapid_crossing_fixture_is_checked_with_clear_endpoints`; `nc_first_feed_crossing_target_is_checked_with_clear_endpoints` |
| Remove unknown-start guard | `nc_unknown_start_refuses_straights_and_arcs_in_simulation_and_playback` |
| Remove taper-tip guard | `nc_flat_and_ball_taper_tips_are_refused_from_every_tool_source` |
| Remove shared fidelity guard | All six fidelity pins below |

The fidelity mutation failed these pins:

- `nc_reduced_target_tightens_simulation_and_playback_even_with_explicit_tolerance`
- `nc_reduced_stock_tightens_simulation_and_playback_without_document_target`
- `nc_unknown_target_and_fixture_refuse_simulation_and_playback_with_explicit_tolerance`
- `nc_unknown_stock_refuses_even_when_target_and_fixtures_are_overridden`
- `nc_unverifiable_reduced_target_cannot_be_bypassed_by_a_large_tolerance`
- `nc_legacy_stock_with_a_missing_source_refuses_simulation_and_playback`

## Final-head validation

Head: `7b01e1ebebe7194501a4b501cafcaf14d5b9693d`.
Quick base: `upstream/main` at `6898b02ea3195e9124e6113afd6ab3cee38d0c50`.
Heavy base, fetched between gates: `upstream/main` at `2394b5ad1efc573b7b99a898a02cc4225b4d9893`.

- `env RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -j12 -p camcraft-app --test stock_sim_document -- --test-threads=12`: 29 passed, 0 failed after mutation restoration.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 1014 steps, 1013 passed and one `wire_post` environment failure, 0 stalls, 27.8 minutes. The failed-step rerun passed one step and 37 tests in 19 seconds. It used `TMPDIR=/tmp/camcraft-4470-tests.THHWZJ` and `--failed gate-logs/quick-20261128-000720`. All 1014 steps have passing coverage. No source changed between runs. Stale seeded metadata was repaired with package-specific target cleanup before the completed full run; no code fix was needed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed. The final quick gate also passed all-crate clippy.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 125 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 42.6 minutes. Three declared known-failure steps for #1950 failed as expected and were accepted by the gate: motion `the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock`, motion `the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`, and app `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`. These are expected failures, not newly passing tests.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 11 twins, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 4.0 minutes.
- Catalog suites passed: `app suites: example_catalog`, `app suites: example_catalog_adaptive`, `app suites: example_catalog_edge_work`. `app heavy: example_catalog` also passed in 9 seconds.
- UI screenshots: not applicable. No UI file changed.

## Goldens moved

None. The three ordinary catalog suites and the reached heavy catalog suite passed. No `.nc`, `.cl` or catalog file changed. The committed worktree is clean.

## Not exercised

- Klartext input through `parse_klartext`.
- Part alignment and a multi-setup document. The runner reads one caller-selected setup.
- `G28`/`G53` reference moves through `ParseOptions::references`.
- A mounted `.mch` read from the document. The machine pin supplies an override; document loading uses `machine::of_setup`.
- Graph update: `graphify` is absent from `PATH`. No package was installed.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: Simulate an external G-code program against the setup stock, target model, fixtures and machine, with each finding on its NC line (`app::nc_sim`).

Fixes #2218

title: fix(tools): holder form shows the outline's largest diameter; a covered body is not read back smaller
body:
## What changed

The cause of the mismatch is a label, not a wrong outline. A second defect under the safety floor was found during the work and is fixed here too. The MCP tool `edit_user_holder` (PR #4438, merged to `main` at `b6089ea6e`) gets the same fix.

1. **The label.** The holder form field `Largest diameter` held the body steel below the flange. For a BT40 ER32 that is the ER32 nut, Ø50. The drawing and the read-only view of a built-in holder show the largest diameter of the whole outline. For a BT40 ER32 that is the BT40 flange, Ø63. The outline was correct in the two views.
   - The editable field is now `Body diameter`.
   - A new read-only row `Largest diameter` shows the value of the drawing (`holder_drawing::largest_d`). This value is 2 x the largest radius of the outline.
2. **A body that the outline does not show (safety floor).** A shrink-fit body that the flange envelope covers shows nowhere in the outline. `HolderShape::of` then read back the narrowest body that draws the outline (the Ø38.748558 for a Ø44 body that PR #4438 saw). A copy of "BT40 Shrink 20 mm" read back a body of Ø41.544, not the table body Ø42. When the user then set a longer gauge length, Apply drew the body smaller than the steel.
   - `HolderShape::of` now returns `None` when a wider body or a narrower nose draws the same outline. The holder then opens in the generic component editor, as an outline from elsewhere does.
   - There is no exception for a copy of a library shrink chuck. A user holder with a wider hidden body can draw the same outline as a library chuck, and the component records no library source. A read-back of the library body would then be smaller than the steel of that holder. 44 of the 117 built-in shrink chucks have a covered body at their library gauge length (for example "BT40 Shrink 20 mm"). Their copies open in the generic component editor. The other 73 (for example "BT40 Shrink 25 mm") open in the form with the table values.
   - The new `HolderShape::component` builds the kind and the geometry. It refuses (`ShapeError::NotKept`, "give a longer gauge length") a shape whose outline does not read back as the same values. The form check and Apply use it. Thus the form never writes an outline that it cannot show again.
3. **`edit_user_holder` (MCP).** `crates/app/src/mcp/holder_shape_tools.rs` now builds through `HolderShape::component`, as the form does. It refuses `NotKept` with the same text as the form. It refuses a held holder with a covered body ("no holder shape outline"), and nothing changes. The test fixture moves from gauge 80 (a covered body) to gauge 120, where the Ø44 body shows. The shape edit goes to gauge 130 and body Ø46. The tool description and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` name the new refusal.

The decision record is in `docs/decisions/4455-holder-largest-diameter.md`. It records what was dropped: the library exception of the first form of this PR, and a "from the library" marker (a project file change, not done without the maintainer).

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-tools` lib: `holder_library::shape::tests::a_body_the_flange_envelope_covers_is_not_read_back_smaller`. It now also pins the look-alike: a BT40 bore 20 holder with a hidden Ø50 body draws the outline of "BT40 Shrink 20 mm", and neither outline reads back as Ø42.
- `camcraft-tools` lib: `holder_library::shape::tests::each_builtin_taper_holder_reads_back_as_its_shape`. Each built-in taper holder reads back with its exact table steel, or it is a shrink chuck whose body the envelope covers (a wider body draws the same outline). The write of the values read keeps the outline.
- `camcraft-tools` lib: `holder_library::shape::tests::an_edited_outline_is_never_smaller_than_the_steel` (each shape reads back exactly, or the write is refused).
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `egui_app::tests::tool_library_holder_largest::a_copied_holder_shows_the_largest_diameter_of_its_outline_and_applies_as_it_is`. It copies BT40 ER32, BT40 Weldon 12 mm and BT40 Shrink 25 mm. It checks that the form value equals 2 x the largest outline radius (63.00 for the BT40 ER32), and that Apply with no edit makes no undo step and keeps the geometry byte for byte. A copy of BT40 Shrink 20 mm opens in the generic editor.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `egui_app::tests::tool_library_holder_form::*` (fixture at gauge 120, edit to gauge 130).
- `camcraft-app` `tool_library_holders`: `holder_shape_mcp::mcp_edit_user_holder_refuses_a_body_the_flange_envelope_covers` (new), `holder_shape_mcp::mcp_edits_a_user_holder_by_its_shape_in_one_undo_step`, `holder_shape_mcp::mcp_edit_user_holder_refuses_by_name_and_changes_nothing`.
- `camcraft-app` `mcp_doc_drift`: `the_committed_reference_matches_the_live_tool_table`.

`#[test]` count of `crates/ui`: 2009 before, 2010 after.

## Screenshots

A copy of the built-in "BT40 ER32", opened in the holder form. Before: the field "Largest diameter" reads 50.0, and the drawing shows Ø 63.00. After: "Body diameter" reads 50.0, and the read-only "Largest diameter" reads 63.00, the same value as the drawing.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4469/er32-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4469/er32-after.png) |

A copy of the built-in "BT40 Shrink 20 mm". Before: the form reads the body back as 41.544, smaller than the table body Ø42. The "after" image is from head `a16b70041`, where the library exception read the body as 42.0. On the final head the exception is removed, so this copy opens in the generic component editor (pinned by the UI test above). No new image was made for that.

title: feat(gcode): the Klartext reader reads RND, CHF and polar LP / CP
body:
## What changed

This is the third slice of the HEIDENHAIN Klartext reader in `camcraft-gcode` (#2227). The reader now reads the contour elements that a hand-written or other-CAM program uses most:

- `RND R<r> [F<f>]` (rounding arc) and `CHF <l> [F<f>]` (chamfer) between two straight feed lines (`L` or `LP`) in the working plane. The reader looks one block ahead. A line that an `RND` / `CHF` follows waits. The line after the transition sets the cut-back points. The toolpath then gets the shortened line, the transition element and the next line. A transition that takes exactly the whole line leaves no line: the reader writes no zero-length feed move. The corner point is not machined. The rounding arc is tangent to both lines, with the tangent length R tan(phi/2). The chamfer cuts the side length from each line. The `F` of the transition acts only on the transition.
- `LP PR.. PA.. [Z..] F../FMAX` with `IPR` / `IPA`: a straight line to polar coordinates about the pole `CC`. A polar coordinate that is not written, and the base of `IPR` / `IPA`, is the last programmed `PR` / `PA` about the current pole. The reader keeps that value only while it knows it exactly: after an `LP` (or a `CP`) about the same pole, with no X/Y move by another block and no move of the pole. When the reader does not know the value, it refuses the `LP` by name and line, for example "LP without PR: the last polar radius about this pole is not known (write PR)". The same rule applies to `PA`.
- `CP PA.. DR±` and `CP IPA.. DR±`, with `Z` / `IZ` as a helix. The reader splits each `CP` into pieces of at most 90 degrees on the same circle, with Z linear over the sweep.

The reader refuses by name, line and block number what it cannot show exactly:

- a transition next to an arc, a cycle, the program start or end, an `FMAX` line, a line with a Z change, a line with a block-end M function (before) or any M function (after);
- a transition that needs more of a line than the line has (also after an earlier cut-back), and two lines in line;
- `CP` with `IPA` and `DR` of different signs, `CP PA` at the start angle, `CP` from the pole, an `LP` whose last programmed `PR` or `PA` is not known (after a Cartesian move or a moved `CC`), an `LP` angle out of range;
- `RL` / `RR` (the message now says why: the tool radius of the tool table and the corner rules of the control are not in the program), `APPR` / `DEP`, `CTP`, `LBL` / `CALL LBL` and inch programs stay refused.

The decisions are in `docs/decisions/2227-klartext-reader.md`, section "third slice".

New files: `crates/gcode/src/klartext/corner.rs`, `crates/gcode/src/klartext/polar.rs`, and the test modules `crates/gcode/tests/klartext/contours.rs` and `crates/gcode/tests/klartext/polar.rs` in the existing `klartext` directory suite (no new test binary).

## Pinning tests

All in the `klartext` suite of `camcraft-gcode`:

- `klartext_rnd_rounds_a_right_angle_with_its_own_feed` (cut-back points, arc centre, the F of RND only on the arc, line map)
- `klartext_chf_and_rnd_chain_on_right_turns` (chamfer, then a rounding on the shortened line, clockwise)
- `klartext_rnd_on_an_obtuse_corner_is_tangent_to_both_lines` (radius and tangency at both ends)
- `klartext_rnd_between_l_and_lp_lines`
- `klartext_rnd_on_the_first_move_of_a_section_starts_at_the_line_start`
- `klartext_transition_elements_refuse_what_is_not_exact`
- `klartext_lp_reaches_polar_points_about_the_pole`
- `klartext_cp_arcs_about_the_pole_in_both_directions` (also `CT` after `CP`)
- `klartext_cp_with_iz_is_a_helix_split_into_quarter_turns`
- `klartext_polar_blocks_refuse_what_is_not_exact`
- `klartext_lp_refuses_a_polar_coordinate_that_it_does_not_know` (new: after a Cartesian `L`, a `C` arc or a moved `CC`; `IPR` / `IPA` without a known base)
- `klartext_lp_keeps_the_last_polar_coordinates_where_they_are_known` (new: a Z-only move, the same `CC` again, an M block; `CP` keeps `PR`; `CP PA` sets `PA`; `CP IPA` from an unknown angle; `LP PR+0`)
- `klartext_lp_angle_out_of_range_is_refused` (new)
- `klartext_transition_that_takes_the_whole_line_leaves_no_zero_length_move` (new: `CHF` that takes the line before, `CHF` that takes the line after, `RND` that takes both)
- `klartext_rnd_after_a_line_with_m3_or_m8` (new)
- `klartext_chf_between_an_l_and_an_lp_line` (new)
- `klartext_transition_with_fmax_is_refused` (new)
- `klartext_contour_with_every_slice_3_element_parses`
- `klartext_seeded_mutations_of_the_contour_never_panic` and the truncation test `klartext_every_truncation_of_the_golden_is_refused_without_a_panic`, now also over the contour program
- `klartext_functions_outside_the_slice_are_refused_by_name_and_block` (updated: `CTP` and `RL` in `LP` replace the `LP` / `CP` rows)

## Gate

Pre-review fixes on top of `3c24051af` (commits `55386f6bd` and `755d7dce2`). All results are on the final head `755d7dce2`, on the winbuild lane (`lanes --branch`, `--needs gcode`), in one lane run. Log `gate-4468-755d7dc.log`.

- Quick gate, `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (`main` at `2394b5a`): 3 steps, 0 failed. `gcode build`, `gcode suites: lib` and `gcode suites: klartext` are ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-gcode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-gcode --test klartext`: 54 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. Each pinning test above is named in the output.
- The first run on `55386f6bd` had one red test: `klartext_lp_keeps_the_last_polar_coordinates_where_they_are_known`. The test read a move by its index, but an `LP` that ends at the tool position adds no move. Commit `755d7dce2` corrects the test. The reader code did not change.
- Light lane: not run. The diff is only in `camcraft-gcode`, and no light twin covers it. P7: no heavy step.

## Not exercised

- No comparison against a real control. Our sources do not say what the control keeps as the last `PR` / `PA` after a Cartesian move or a moved `CC`. The reader refuses those cases. It does not guess.
- No comparison against a real control for the geometry either. The geometry comes from the published manual behaviour and plane geometry.
- A transition next to an arc, `CTP`, `APPR` / `DEP`, `RL` / `RR`, `LBL` / `CALL LBL` and inch programs are refused, not read. They stay open on #2227.
- No consumer of the reader changes. The example catalog suites do not apply: no post and no toolpath generator changed.

Changelog: The Klartext reader reads RND and CHF between straight lines, polar LP and CP about CC, and the CP helix; it refuses by name what it cannot show exactly.

Effort: max

Refs #2227
