title: fix(xtask): join the UI config directory by components for Windows
body:
## What changed

- `unit_env::plan_notes` builds the UI directory as `root.join("crates").join("ui")`. Before, it used `root.join("crates/ui")`.
- The test `plan_notes_only_scan_ui_config_for_ui_steps` builds its expected config path by components too.
- A new source pin, `plan_notes_join_the_ui_directory_by_components`, keeps the production join in that form.
- A decision file: `docs/decisions/4454-win-ui-config-path.md`.

## Cause

On Windows, `Path::join("crates/ui")` keeps the `/` in the path. The note showed `...\crates/ui\.cargo\config.toml`. The test expected `...\crates/ui/.cargo\config.toml`. The strings did not match, so the test failed on Windows only. Linux uses `/` everywhere, so Linux and macOS passed.

## Tests

- Pin: `unit_env::tests::plan_notes_join_the_ui_directory_by_components`. It fails on unchanged code on Linux: `plan_notes must join crates and ui as two components`.
- Mutation: I put the old join back. The pin failed. I restored the fix. The pin passed.
- `plan_notes_only_scan_ui_config_for_ui_steps` passes on Linux before and after. Its Windows failure cannot show on Linux.
- `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask unit_env::`: 15 passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: 1 step (`xtask unit tests`), 0 failed, 339 s.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: one error, in `xtask/src/unit_sweep.rs:67` (`clippy::needless_bool`). This PR does not touch that file. The same error is on upstream/main `1cf7390dc`. The changed lines in this PR give no lint.

## Goldens moved

None. The diff changes no recorded program. It touches only `xtask/` and `docs/decisions/`. I did not run `example_catalog`, because the diff cannot reach it.

- I did not run the test on Windows. No Windows host is available to this worker. The Windows check watcher of main will confirm it after the merge.
- #4427 and #4428 have the same kind of separator failure in `unit_env/config.rs` tests. This PR does not fix them.

None. No open PR changes `xtask/src/unit_env.rs`.

title: feat(ui): 3D tool preview flutes for each kind, a finer mesh, part inks
body:
## What changed

- **Flutes for each kind.** The 3D preview of the tool library cuts flutes into each kind that has a cutting part with flutes (`flutes::fluted_kind`): end mill, ball nose, bull nose, chamfer (`Taper`), twist drill, tap, both thread mills, T-slot, keyseat, dovetail, lollipop and form mill. The lathe tools, the probe, the electrode and the beam and wire tools stay plain. The flute lines of the side view use the same rule.
- **Counts.** The #3908 rule stays: a tool with no flute count draws no flutes. Two display defaults are new. A twist drill with no count draws 2 flutes at a 30 degree helix (DIN 338 type N). A tap with no count draws 3 straight flutes. The shipped drills and taps state no count. The tool keeps no count, and nothing is written.
- **Thread mills.** The flutes are cut into the toothed steel of #4451. The Properties side preview (`tool_preview::paint` without a steel override) also draws the teeth now (`thread_form::toothed`).
- **Finer mesh.** The preview revolve (`tool_library_dialog::model::RING`) has 96 facets around, not 32. The collision and body meshes do not change. The model is built only when its input changes. The screen mesh is projected only when the mesh, its parts, the rect, the orbit or the part inks change. A still frame builds nothing.
- **Three part inks.** Three new theme tokens in `crates/ui-kit`: `tool_model_flute` (gold), `tool_model_shank` (steel grey) and `tool_model_holder` (slate blue). They are in the theme struct, both tables, the legal check, the names, the overlay, the gallery lists, `assets/themes/theme.json.example` and `docs/user-guide/themes.md`. The dark and light columns have the same values, as the other tool inks do: the previews keep their own dark ground. Each facet has the ink of its part, shaded by the light (45 % edge-on to 100 %). title: feat(ui): Holders page imports and exports holder files
body:
## What changed

The Holders page buttons **Import…** and **Export…** are enabled. Each has a hover text that says what it does.

- **Export…** writes the user holders of the document to a holder file (`.camcomponents`). The file uses the component library format (`component_library::to_text`, `camcraft-components/1`). A user holder is a holder row of the component table whose id is not `builtin:`. A holder is an adaptive item with a spindle taper on its machine side, the same set that the Holders page lists.
- **Import…** reads such a file and adds each holder as a user holder, without a library link, in one undo step. The new undoable command is `ImportHolders` (`crates/app/src/commands/holder_file.rs`). A row keeps its file id when the id is free. An id that the document, the component library or an earlier row holds gets a new `user:holder:<name>` id, then ` (2)`, ` (3)`, as "Copy as user holder" does.
- A file that is not correct is refused by name, and the document does not change. This includes bad JSON, a truncated file, a wrong envelope, a file with no row, a row that is not a holder, and a holder outline that is not correct (a negative radius, fewer than 3 points). The refusal shows on the Tool pane.
- MCP: the new tools `export_holders` and `import_holders` (`crates/app/src/mcp/holder_file_tools.rs`) use the same function and the same command. `export_holders` asks for file-write approval in a live session (`mcp/live.rs`). `import_holders` refuses by name when the component library cannot be read, because then it cannot keep the new ids clear of the library ids. It does not use the built-in ids only. The generated reference `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the guide row in `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` name the two tools.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/4389-holder-files.md` (the format, the id rule, the refusals).

`tool_library_dialog/mod.rs` is not changed.

## Screenshots

Before (main): the two buttons are disabled, and the hover names #4389.

After: the two buttons are enabled, and the hover says what Import does.

Head `933e1774d`. One `lanes` run (`--needs app --pool`, Mac lane). Log: `gate-4463-933e1774d.log`, first line `head 933e1774d0f430f683c7e7e6f99ba5fdf796e4da`.

title: feat(gcode): the Klartext reader reads tapping cycles 206/207, the cycle 9 dwell and cycle 32
body:
## What changed

This PR is the second slice of the HEIDENHAIN Klartext (`.H`) reader in `camcraft-gcode` (first slice: #4361). The reader now reads back every block that our Klartext post writes today (#4395 cycles; #4442 cycle 32).

- New module `crates/gcode/src/klartext/taps.rs`: `CYCL DEF 206` (tapping with a floating tap holder) and `CYCL DEF 207` (rigid tapping).
  - Motion of both cycles: rapid to the set-up clearance, feed to the thread depth, feed back out to the set-up clearance, rapid to the 2nd set-up clearance when it is higher. This is the G84 chain of `cycle_expand`.
  - 206 reads Q200, Q201, Q206, Q211, Q203, Q204. Q211 is the dwell at the bottom (`cl::Cycle` dwell). The record is `CycleKind::FloatingTap`.
  - 207 reads Q200, Q201, Q239, Q203, Q204. The feed is S x Q239 with the S that is active at the call. The record is `CycleKind::Tap`.
- New module `crates/gcode/src/klartext/old_cycles.rs`: the sub-block cycles.
  - `CYCL DEF 9.0` / `9.1 DWELL <s>`: one `DwellEvent` at the `9.1` block (the cycle is DEF-active).
  - `CYCL DEF 32.0` / `32.1 [T<mm>]` / optional `32.2 HSC-MODE:<0|1> [TA<deg>]`: checked, no change to the path.
  - The order of the sub-blocks is enforced. A block between `9.0` and `9.1` (or `32.0` and `32.1`) is refused with its line and block number.
- `cycles.rs`: the cycle definition has a `HoleShape` (drill, floating tap, rigid tap). The Q-list check and the hole levels are shared helpers now.
- `cl::Cycle::entry_z` of a Klartext hole cycle is now the surface Q203. The first slice wrote the set-up clearance. Q203 is what the post's CL stream records as `ENTRY`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2227-klartext-reader.md`, new section "second slice".

### Refused (by name, with the line; the message starts with `block N:`)

- `CYCL DEF 207` with a negative Q239 (left-hand thread): `CYCL DEF 207 Q239`. The control turns the spindle against M3 for it, and the reader output has only the modal spindle direction.
- `CYCL DEF 207` called without a spindle speed S above 0 (invalid cycle).
- Q parameters that a cycle does not have, missing required ones, Q201 not negative, negative clearances, a zero pitch, a zero feed, a negative or too long dwell.
- Sub-block cycles other than 9 and 32 (`CYCL DEF 1.0`, `7.0`, `10.0`, ...).
- All other functions of the first slice stay refused (`RND`, `CHF`, `LP`, `CP`, `APPR`, `DEP`, `LBL`, `CALL`, `RL`, `RR`, INCH programs, ...).

## Tests

All tests are in the existing directory suite `crates/gcode/tests/klartext` (two new sub-modules, no new top-level binary).

Pinning tests:

- `klartext_cycle_golden_reads_back_into_the_stream_motion_and_cycles`: the recorded golden `picomax_cycles.nc` reads back into the motion of its CL stream `cycles.cnc` (5 sections: drill, peck, deep with dwell, rigid tap, floating tap). Each stream section is a contiguous run of the read moves, and the moves between the runs are rapid approach moves above the section start. The cycle records match the stream `CYCLE` lines (kind, XY, R, bottom, entry, dwell). The cycle 9 dwell is 0.3 s after the last infeed.
- `klartext_every_post_golden_reads_back_without_a_refused_block`: each `.nc` file in `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/heidenhain-klartext/` parses. No block is refused, so the list of refused blocks is empty. When #4442 merges, its `picomax_smoothing.nc` comes into this test automatically.
- `klartext_cycle_207_taps_at_s_times_pitch_and_feeds_out_to_the_set_up_clearance`
- `klartext_cycle_206_feeds_at_q206_with_the_bottom_dwell_at_each_m99`
- `klartext_cycle_207_needs_a_spindle_speed_at_the_call`
- `klartext_tapping_cycle_definitions_are_checked_by_name_and_block`
- `klartext_cycle_9_dwells_where_it_is_defined`
- `klartext_cycle_32_is_checked_and_leaves_the_path_unchanged`
- `klartext_sub_block_cycles_must_be_complete_and_in_order`
- Degenerate input: `klartext_every_truncation_of_the_golden_is_refused_without_a_panic` now covers both goldens; new `klartext_seeded_mutations_of_the_cycle_golden_never_panic` (3000 seeded mutations, time limit); `klartext_bad_numbers_are_refused` has 4 more cases.

## Gate results

Head `16f638efb`, base `origin/main` 1cf7390dc, Windows lane `winbuild` (lanes, `--needs gcode`), `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=5`. Log: `gate-2227-16f638efb.log` (first line `head 16f638efbddaa88ea035771762e44eacd097921f`).

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: gcode build (`--no-run`) | ok (13 s) |
| gcode suites: lib | ok |
| gcode suites: klartext (whole suite, all pinning tests above) | ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-gcode --all-targets -- -D warnings` | ok |
| Example catalog suites | not applicable: no post and no toolpath generator changed |
| Light lane / heavy lanes | not run: no crate depends on `camcraft-gcode`, so the diff reaches no `app` or `motion` lane and no light twin |

## Not exercised

- No real TNC-written program was read. The hand-written test programs follow the public manual syntax.
- The golden of #4442 (`picomax_smoothing.nc`) is not on `main` yet. Cycle 32 is tested with hand-written blocks in the same form as the post writes them.
- No app command, MCP tool or CLI verb reads `.H` files yet. This PR adds no user-facing command, so no MCP tool is necessary.
- Still open on #2227: `LBL` / `CALL LBL`, `RND` / `CHF`, polar `LP` / `CP`, `APPR` / `DEP`, inch programs, `RL` / `RR`, left-hand rigid tapping. The reader refuses each of them by name.

Changelog: camcraft-gcode reads HEIDENHAIN Klartext tapping cycles 206 and 207, the cycle 9 dwell and the cycle 32 tolerance, so every program that the Klartext post writes reads back.

Refs #2227

body:
## What changed

The Recipes tab of the tool library window now has two inputs for each material row, under the table:

- **Surface speed** (Vc, m/min; sfm in an inch document).
- **Chip load** (fz, mm per tooth; inch in an inch document).

A Vc edit sets the stored spindle rpm of the row: n = Vc x 1000 / (pi x D). An fz edit sets the stored feed of the row: F = fz x z x n. The rpm stays. The table shows the new rpm or feed immediately, and the inputs show the values that follow from the table. The derived line of #4337 is now the hover text of the two inputs.

- The stored values do not change. The project file does not change.
- The edits write the draft of the window only. The one Apply of the editor lands them as one `ChangeTool`, one undo step. No command is new, so no MCP tool is necessary.
- The chip load input is disabled when the tool has no flute count, or when the row has no rpm. The surface speed input is disabled when the tool diameter is not above zero. The disabled input gives the reason in its hover text. The conversion functions return the reason as an error, so nothing divides by zero.

title: fix(ui): the tool library preview draws a thread mill's teeth
body:
## What changed

The tool library window drew a thread mill as a large plain cylinder. The 3D model and the side view used `Tool::profile`. That profile is the crest cylinder over the full cutting length, because the reach laws read that envelope (#894).

- New display-only module `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_library_dialog/thread_form.rs`. It draws the cutting length of a thread mill as its teeth:
  - the core at the tooth roots: the crest radius minus the external ISO root depth (`EXTERNAL_DEPTH_PER_PITCH` x pitch);
  - one V tooth of the stated form angle for each row: `thread_mill::rows` rows on a multi-form mill, one tooth over the stated tooth height on a single-form mill;
  - the steel above the cutting length stays: the shank of `Tool::profile`, or the neck of a landed drawn cutter.
- `model.rs` calls `thread_form::toothed` on the steel outline (one line). The 3D mesh and the side view of the window both read that outline.
- Every point stays inside the crest cylinder, so the plain mesh's box does not change.
- A thread mill has no neck field: a neck comes from the drawn cutter outline (`thread_mill.rs`). The PR keeps that model. The decision is in `docs/decisions/4451-thread-mill-preview.md`.

Display only. `Tool::profile`, the collision envelope, toolpaths, simulation and posted output do not change. No command changes, so no MCP tool is necessary.

## Pinning tests

- `a_multi_form_thread_mill_draws_one_tooth_per_row_on_its_core` (8 crests at the cutting diameter, the roots at the core, the teeth end on the core at the cutting length)
- `a_single_form_thread_mill_draws_one_tooth_then_its_neck` (one tooth, then a drawn 4 mm neck keeps its diameter and length, then the shank)

body:
## What changed

This is wave 1 of #3190. It folds the 18 flat `crates/app/tests/turning_*.rs` binaries into the `turning` directory suite.

- The 18 files move to `crates/app/tests/turning/<name>.rs` (git renames, 99-100 % similar).
- `turning.rs` loads each file with `#[path = "turning/<name>.rs"] mod turning_<name>;`.
- Each module keeps its old binary name. The test `turning_bore` / `x` is now `turning` / `turning_bore::x`.
- Each submodule keeps its `//!` header, its Gate map and its lane line. `xtask` joins the Gate maps of all sources of a suite (`quick::gate_maps`).
- `mod common;` becomes `use crate::common;`. Four files declared `common` and did not use it. Those lines are removed.
- Two `include_str!` paths get one more `../`, because the files are one directory deeper.
- `docs/decisions/3190-fold-turning-suite.md` records the choice of the wave and what was dropped.

No production code changes. No test body changes.

## Cause

Each `camcraft-app` test binary is about 100-130 MB. The turning domain had 19 binaries for 115 tests.

## Tests

This is a test-layout refactor. No behaviour changes, so no test can fail before it. The proof is that the test set is the same:

- Before (base `e4b08e95b`): `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test 'turning*' -- --list` gives 19 binaries, 115 tests, 0 ignored.
- After: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test turning -- --list` gives 1 binary, 115 tests, 0 ignored.
- The sorted list of qualified names (`<old binary>::<test>`) before is equal to the sorted list of module paths after (`diff` is empty).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test turning`: 115 passed, 0 failed, in about 6 s. It ran three times, all green.
- Each temp file in these tests has its own prefix and the process id. No two submodules write the same path in the shared process.

Gate on the final head `6939377`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: plan `app:turning whole suite`, 1 step, ok (41 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.

- Trial merge with upstream/main `4d891498e`: clean. Upstream did not change any of the 19 files or `tests/common/` since the base.

Disk (debug, Linux): the 18 old binaries took 2,306 MB. The folded binary takes 201 MB. That is about 2.1 GB less for each worktree.

Note: on this host sccache did not answer for this worktree, so the gates ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`.

- The other domains of #3190. They are for later waves, so the issue stays open (`Refs #3190`).

body:
## What changed

- A new built-in post `FluidNC` (`assets/posts/fluidnc.cps`).
- A new built-in machine `3040 router (FluidNC)` (`assets/machines/fluidnc-3040.mch`). The machine names `FluidNC` as its post.

- `FluidNC` is in `M3_ONLY_POSTS` (`crates/app/src/operation/tool_gate.rs`), because the post writes only `M3`. This is the same as `Grbl 1.1`.
- The posting guide table has a FluidNC row.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/3192-fluidnc-post.md`. Each dialect decision names its FluidNC wiki page.

The post is `grbl.cps` with these differences:
- Line 2 of the header is `(FLUIDNC POST - NOT VERIFIED ON A MACHINE)`. This line stays until the owner reports a clean dry run.
- The refusals and comments name FluidNC.
- The comments cite the FluidNC wiki pages.

The words that the post writes are the same as the Grbl 1.1 words:
- No canned cycles. Drilling is G0 / G1 moves and `G4 P<seconds>`.
- The tool change is `M5`, a Z lift, a comment, then `M0`. The post writes no `M6` and no `T` word. FluidNC's `M6` acts only through a tool changer or a macro in the YAML file, which the post cannot see.
- Tapping, boring and `G41`/`G42` are refused by name.

## Readings

The FluidNC wiki pages could not be fetched in this session (no network permission). The decisions come from FluidNC's documented G-code and M-code lists as the author knows them. The decision file has a table with one row for each point and its wiki page. Please check each row against wiki.fluidnc.com. The owner's AI-made post was not read. title: feat(post): the Klartext post writes smoothing as cycle 32 TOLERANCE
body:
## What changed

The Heidenhain Klartext post (`assets/posts/heidenhain-klartext.cps`) writes a section's smoothing ask (`PARAM Smoothing` / `SmoothingMode`, #616) as cycle 32 TOLERANCE. Before this change, the post refused each smoothing ask. This is the next slice of #4095: the Klartext post now reads the resolver flags `g62Mode` and `g62TMaxUm` (#4226). Until now, only the DIN/ISO post read them.

- The blocks come after `M3` and `M8`/`M9`, before the first move of the section:
  - `CYCL DEF 32.0 TOLERANCE`
  - `CYCL DEF 32.1 T<mm>` (1 µm grid, the same grid as the DIN/ISO `G62`)
  - `CYCL DEF 32.2 HSC-MODE:<0|1> TA0`, only where `g62Mode` permits it: `yes`, or `option2` with option 2 in `installed_options`. `0` is finish, `1` is rough. The post moves no rotary axis, so `TA` is 0.
- The section end resets the cycle with `CYCL DEF 32.0 TOLERANCE` and `CYCL DEF 32.1` (no T), before `M9` and `M5`. Thus no tolerance goes into the next operation.
- The post refuses by name:
  - a T above the largest T of the profile (`g62TMaxUm`);
  - a positive T that rounds to T0 (the control reads T 0 as the machine builder's tolerance);
  - a profile with no cycle 32;
  - a rough ask where `32.2 HSC-MODE` cannot be written (the post sets `failOnWarning`, so a warning would also stop it);
  - a mode with no tolerance, a mode that is not finish or rough, and a tolerance that is not a positive number.
- Source: iTNC 530 Klartext user manual 533 190-22 (NC 340 49x-03), section 8.10 "TOLERANCE (Cycle 32)", pages 509-511. The post header cites this manual already.
- One form is inferred: the manual prints no reset block. The post writes `CYCL DEF 32.1` with no T, which is what the manual's NO ENT answer leaves. This is the same inference as the bare `G62` reset of the DIN/ISO post. The decision file says this.
- Decisions and dropped options: `docs/decisions/4095-klartext-cycle-32.md`.

## Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530, NC 340490-03, profile itnc-49x)

The machine file lists no installed options. Thus:
- a finish ask posts `CYCL DEF 32.0 TOLERANCE` and `CYCL DEF 32.1 T<mm>` only;
- a rough ask is refused: `smoothing mode rough: controller profile itnc-49x takes CYCL DEF 32.2 HSC-MODE only with software option 2 (HSC machining), which the machine file does not list; ask for finish smoothing, or none - refused, not posted`;
- the largest T is 10 mm.

A program with no smoothing ask is byte-identical. The `picomax.nc` and `picomax_cycles.nc` goldens and the refusal goldens did not change.

Example (from the new golden `picomax_smoothing.nc`, a finish ask of 0.02 mm, then a section with no ask):

```
25 M3
26 M9
27 CYCL DEF 32.0 TOLERANCE
28 CYCL DEF 32.1 T0.02
29 L X+10 Y+0 R0 FMAX
...
38 L X+15 Y+0 Z+10 R0 FMAX
39 CYCL DEF 32.0 TOLERANCE
40 CYCL DEF 32.1
41 M9
42 M5
```

## Pinning tests

Binary `script_goldens` (crate `camcraft-post`), suite module `script_heidenhain_klartext`, new module `crates/post/tests/klartext/smoothing_tests.rs` (it joins the existing suite; no new test binary):
- `smoothing_tests::klartext_smoothing_posts_on_the_picomax_golden` (new golden `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/heidenhain-klartext/picomax_smoothing.nc`)
- `smoothing_tests::a_finish_ask_writes_t_only_and_the_section_end_resets_it`
- `smoothing_tests::option_2_writes_hsc_mode_for_finish_and_rough`
- `smoothing_tests::each_klartext_smoothing_refusal_names_its_cause`
- `smoothing_tests::the_t_range_bounds_post_on_the_picomax`
- `unsupported_motion_or_missing_setup_data_is_refused`: its smoothing case is now a rough ask (refused on the Picomax), because a finish ask posts now. The case count is the same.

## Gate results

Final head `bf7c0d068` (it merges `origin/main` `4d891498e`; the merge moved the Klartext suite into `script_goldens`, #3188).

- Mac lane (`--needs app --pool`), log `gate-4095-bf7c0d0-app.log`:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 34 steps, 34 ok, 0 failed, 0 stalled. The plan has `post suites: script_goldens`, the app suites `conformance` and `klartext_builtin`, and `gcode suites: klartext`.
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog --test example_catalog_adaptive --test example_catalog_edge_work --test smoothing`: 47 + 1 + 1 + 8 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- winbuild lane (`camcraft-post`, head `bf7c0d068`), log `gate-4095-bf7c0d0-post.log`: `script_goldens` 445 passed (the five `script_heidenhain_klartext::smoothing_tests::*` tests and `unsupported_motion_or_missing_setup_data_is_refused` included); `cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib heidenhain` 14 passed; clippy `camcraft-post` clean.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): 6 steps, 6 ok. It ran on head `5f791786e` (before the merge of main; the code under test is the same). Log `gate-4095-5f79178-app.log`. On that head, the quick gate had one red step: `example_catalog` `catalog_3d_rough_finish::rebuilds` and `::regenerates` stopped at their 60 s time budget under load (open issue #3975). On the final head the same tests passed.
- The new golden `picomax_smoothing.nc` was written from the post output of a winbuild run and read line by line.

## Not exercised

- No program ran on a real control. The reset form `CYCL DEF 32.1` with no T is inferred from the manual (see above).
- The machine builder must prepare the machine for cycle 32 (the manual says so). The DIN/ISO post already writes `G62` for the Picomax on the same assumption.
- The other Klartext items of #4095 stay open: other iTNC 530 releases (#4114), `TOOL CALL "NAME"`, `FUNCTION DWELL`, and an M91/M92 retract where `m140` is no. The Klartext post still serves NC 340490-03 only.

Changelog: The Heidenhain Klartext post writes a smoothing ask as cycle 32 TOLERANCE (CYCL DEF 32.0/32.1, and 32.2 HSC-MODE where the control profile and its options permit it), and resets it at the end of each operation. Before, it refused smoothing.

Effort: max

Refs #4095

title: fix(gate): the site tests run in the batch and release gates, and in quick when their inputs change
body:
## What changed

The site tests ran only in the `site` job of `release.yml`, after the tag. They were red at three cuts in a row. This PR makes the site green again and runs the site tests in the gate, before the tag.

1. Site (commit 1, `fix(site)`): the site tests were red on `origin/main` 39298012.
   - The ribbon labels moved from `panes.rs` to `panes/cmd.rs` (#4393). `New tool…` moved to `tool_library_dialog/list_header.rs`. The two tutorial tests now read the files that draw the labels. The assertion is the same.
   - `site/static/icons/op-rotary-contour.png` and `op-rotary-parallel.png` drifted from `assets/ui/`. They are copied from `assets/ui/`.
   - The post reference had no row for `manualToolChange` (#4085). The row is new, written from our own contract in `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`.
2. Gate (commit 2, `fix(gate)`): a step kind that does not start cargo, `xtask/src/site_step.rs`.
   - The step `site tests (python unittest, zola, node)` runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests` (else `python`) at the root. It sets `ZOLA` (else `zola` on PATH), `PYTHONUTF8=1` and `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`. `node` must be on PATH. All calls go through `std::process::Command` with clear errors, under the gate watchdog.
   - batch and release: always. quick: when the diff touches a path of `site_step::INPUTS`. A quick fallback to batch gets it too.
   - `Step` has a new field `site: Option<Missing>`. `Run::execute` sends such a step to `site_step::execute` (one line). The step shares the lanes, and `gate batch --lane N/M` gives it to one lane.
   - `site_step::INPUTS` is the one list of inputs: `site/`, `assets/ui/`, `assets/posts/`, `assets/machines/`, `examples/`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/`, and the exact source files that the site tests open.
   - Usage text and the `gate` skill name the step in each tier.
3. Decision: `docs/decisions/4133-site-tests-in-the-gate.md`.

## The site tests on main, before and after

| Tree | Tools | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` 39298012 | zola 0.23.6, no node | 112 tests, 23 failures, 6 errors (the 6 errors are node missing) |
| `origin/main` 39298012 | zola 0.23.6, node 22 | 112 tests, 23 failures |
| this head | zola 0.23.6, node 22 | 112 tests, OK |

## The missing-tool rule

- quick and batch: a missing tool (python 3, zola, node) is a `SKIP` row. The note is `SKIPPED (tool missing: <tool>) - not a pass; install: ...`. The run does not fail for it, but the row is never `ok`.
- release: a missing tool is a `FAIL` row. The note names the tool and its install step. The cut gate is the last check before the tag.
- A zola that is not the pinned 0.23.6 adds a note to the row. It does not fail.

## What the runners need (for the maintainer)

This PR changes no workflow, no trigger and no runner. Each self-hosted runner user needs these tools on its PATH:

- cut runner (`camcraft-cut`): python 3, zola 0.23.6 (or `ZOLA=<path>` in the runner `.env`), node. The zola download and its sha256 are in `release.yml`, step "Install pinned Zola". Without these tools, the cut gate is red at the site step. That is the rule of this PR.
- post-merge runner (`camcraft-post-merge`): the same tools. Without them, the batch summary shows a `SKIP` row for the site step.

Follow-up: #4433. `post-merge-skip.sh` skips a push that changes only `site/static/`, `site/tools/` or `site/templates/`. That is a `.github` change for the maintainer.

## Pins (xtask)

- `site_step_tests::each_path_that_a_site_test_names_is_an_input`: reads each path literal of `site/tests/*.py` (and the `UI + "..."` joins) and fails when `INPUTS` does not cover it.
- `site_step_tests::input_rule_takes_directories_by_prefix_and_files_exactly`
- `site_step_tests::batch_and_release_run_the_site_step_with_their_missing_tool_rule`
- `site_step_tests::quick_runs_the_site_step_only_when_an_input_changed`
- `site_step_tests::a_missing_tool_is_a_skip_row_in_quick_and_batch_and_a_fail_row_in_release`
- `site_step_tests::dry_run_prints_the_command_and_the_rule_and_runs_nothing`
- `site_step_tests::the_note_reads_the_unittest_summary`
- `tests::batch_skips_slow_binaries_and_release_runs_everything` (updated: batch ends with the site step, release has one more step)

## Gate results on this head

Head `9ca89a5ceb7c288b19f552ca44b182bc0ee566b5`, Linux, `-j 6`:

- `cargo test -j 6 -p xtask`: green (381 unit tests and all integration binaries). This is the quick plan step `xtask unit tests`.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green. It was red on Rust 1.100 at `unit_sweep::plain_dir` (`needless_bool`, a false positive of a `#[cfg(windows)]` block); the function is now one expression on each OS, with the same logic.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run`: 2 steps, `xtask unit tests` and `site tests (python unittest, zola, node)` (the diff touches `site/`).
- `cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run` and `gate release --no-snapshots --dry-run`: each prints the site step and its rule.
- `cargo xtask gate batch --only "site tests"` with zola 0.23.6 and node 22: `ok 18s ... Ran 112 tests in 16.631s, OK`.
- The same without zola and node: `SKIP ... SKIPPED (tool missing: zola, node) - not a pass; install: ...`, exit 0.
- `cargo xtask gate release --only "site tests"` without zola and node: `FAIL ... tool missing: zola, node - the release tier needs it; install: ...`, exit 1.
- No light lane and no example catalog suites: no post, toolpath or crate code changed.

## Not exercised

- Windows and macOS: the code uses only `std::process::Command` and `/`-free arguments, but it was not built or run there.
- The cut runner and the post-merge runner: not run. Their tools are not verified.
- The `--lane N/M` form was not run for real (pinned by `lane_split::assign` in a test).

Process change: yes

Effort: high (no escalation)

Changelog: none

Fixes #4133

title: feat(mcp): edit_user_holder edits a user holder by its shape fields
body:
## What changed

- New MCP tool `edit_user_holder` in `crates/app/src/mcp/holder_shape_tools.rs`. It edits a holder of the document's component table by its shape fields: `taper`, `clamp`, `bore`, `gauge_len`, `nose_d`, `largest_d` and `name`. Only `id` is required.
- The tool reads the held shape with `HolderShape::of`. It puts the stated fields over that shape. It builds the kind and the outline with `HolderShape::kind` and `HolderShape::geometry(ADAPTIVE_PORT)`, as the holder form's Apply does. Then it runs one `EditDocumentComponent` through the History. This is the same undoable command as the GUI. The existing MCP `undo` and `redo` invert it.
- The refusals are the same as in the form:
  - a value that cannot describe steel: `holder not changed: <ShapeError text>`;
  - a broken fit: the command's refusal, which names the component and the tool;
  - an empty name: `the holder needs a name`;
  - an edit that changes nothing: the command's "already so".
- The tool also refuses an id that the document does not hold, an unknown taper or clamp, and a holder whose outline is not a shape outline. The last refusal points to `upsert_tool_component`.
- An ER or Weldon clamp without a stated `largest_d` takes `nose_d`, because these clamps have one body diameter.
- Registration: one `.chain` line in `component_tools::all()` and one `mod` line in `mcp/mod.rs`.
- The generated reference `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the guide `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` name the tool (the `mcp_doc_drift` tests require this).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/4391-mcp-edit-user-holder.md`.

## The camcraft-mcp skill row

The skill is a process file. This PR does not change it. Issue #4432 (`P5`, `effort:low`) holds the proposed row, word for word.

## Pinning tests

New file `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/holder_shape_mcp.rs`, in the existing `tool_library_holders` directory suite (no new test binary):

- `mcp_edits_a_user_holder_by_its_shape_in_one_undo_step`: a change, its outline (equal to `HolderShape::geometry` of the stated shape), the tool derived again (gauge length +10 mm), one undo, one redo, and an unstated field that keeps its value.
- `mcp_edit_user_holder_refuses_by_name_and_changes_nothing`: the `ShapeError` refusals, the broken fit (names the component and the tool), a holder that is not a shape outline, an unknown id, clamp, taper and argument, an empty name, an edit that changes nothing. After these, the holder row and the tool are unchanged.

## Gate (final head `f5b1eccd0`)

Log `gate-4391-f5b1eccd0.log` (first line `head f5b1eccd0a873141c9f7b423e423a8eeb7ce567e`), one lanes run on mac-1:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 169 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (24.5 min). The step `app suites: tool_library_holders` ran the whole suite, with both pinning tests: ok.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_doc_drift`: 9 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The first head (`891163f75`) had one red pinning test: the fit-refusal call did not state `largest_d` (see "Not exercised"). Commit `f5b1eccd0` corrects the test call. The tool code did not change.

## Not exercised

- The GUI. The holder form is not changed.
- No post, toolpath or geometry code is changed. No example catalog run and no light lane run: nothing under them changed.
- `HolderShape::of` reads back the largest diameter of the test holder as Ø38.748558 mm, not the Ø44 mm that built it (the body is under the flange envelope). The outline is the same, so the read-back is correct. A call that changes the nose diameter on a shrink holder should state `largest_d`.

Changelog: MCP: `edit_user_holder` edits a user holder by its shape fields (taper, clamp, bore, gauge length, nose and largest diameter) in one undo step, as the holder form does.

Effort: medium (not escalated)

Fixes #4391

title: fix(pathkernel): no silent recovery from a rejected result
body:
Side branch: side/path-kernel

Fixes class B and the minor items of the review of PR #4383 (2026-11-27T18:06:55Z, head `7cd322966`). Issue #4407. Writer: worker K-fixB (record https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4407#issuecomment-7225214161).

## The rule that closes the class

Never recover in silence from a refused or rejected result. Each place refuses by a name of its own stage, or it records the fallback with a note (or a named `Fallback`) that names the failed check. The decisions are in `docs/decisions/4407-pathkernel-dependency-edges.md`.

## Class B: each item and its commit

| Item of the review | Result | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| `region_build.rs:132-134` unoriented centre made normal again | **Refuse**: the re-normalisation is removed; `PlanarRegion::new` refuses with `NOT_ORIENTED`. A public value still cannot reach it (geometry gives normal regions), so the guard is pinned on the loops (unit test) | 268fa07c5 |
| `entry/stage.rs:178-183` ABOVE dropped | **Named fallback / note**: `ABOVE` is public; it is the reason of the named fallback where `needs_fallback` asks for one, else a note that says which asked kind is not flown | efe0ba7f0 |
| `entry/exit.rs:54-64` `Exit::new` admits a low retract | **Refuse, one checked path**: `Exit::new(lead_out, retract, top)` and `Exit::proved` call the same `check_retract` (`RAPID_IN_MATERIAL` under the top, `BAD_EXIT` for a value that is not finite). The callers in `tests/laws/` (`construction.rs`, `exit.rs`, `plan.rs`, `standins.rs`) and `kernel_emit/tests.rs` pass the top of their fixtures. The converter also refuses a retract under the clearance height (next row) | d3e849dca, 81a919838 |
| `kernel_emit/pen.rs:140-149`, `:268-271` low retract clamped | **Refuse**: `EXIT_UNDER_CLEARANCE` (and `NOT_FINITE`) | d62277264 |
| `entry/exit.rs:115-136` lead-out dropped with no note | **Named fallback**: `Exit::fallback()` (arc lead-out -> straight retract, `NO_LEAD_OUT_ROOM` / `NO_END_DIRECTION` / the lead refusal); the converter writes it to the notes. A room with an area that `Area::new` refuses is a refusal | d3e849dca, d62277264 |
| `.ok()` in `entry/material.rs:117,128`, `entry/air.rs:103,111,115`, `entry/hole.rs:26,28`, `entry/column.rs:37,40` | **Named in notes or refusal**: `Ctx::checked` keeps kind and reason; a note of the entry that fits, or `Refusal::after`/`tried()` of the final refusal (text: `; tries refused: ...`). Also: `Ctx::holds` and the air clip refuse a geometry error; a non-finite helix point is refused | efe0ba7f0 |
| `load/trochoid.rs:188` | The line is the clamp of the asked pitch to the engagement limit (not an `.ok()`). **Note**: the load verdict says the limited pitch | abdb94e15 |
| `kernel_emit/arcs.rs:58-60` empty arc as `ARC_NOT_MONOTONE` | **Refuse by its own reason**: `ARC_EMPTY` | d62277264 |

The search of the rest of the class (kernel crate and `kernel_emit/`):
- `load/rings.rs:105` dropped a ring piece that `Curve::new` refused: now only a piece too short to be a curve is skipped; each other refusal is a refusal (268fa07c5).
- Kept, with the reason in the decision file: the link stage (an unproved chord or approach is a lift with a named `LiftReason`), `load/law.rs` (`material_at` = `None` counts as material, the `StockRead` contract), index `unwrap_or` on lists of the same length, `unwrap_or_default` on the first point of a curve that has points by construction, `air_zone` (its limit is already a note).

## Notes of the review

| Note | Result | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| `geo2d/medial.rs` finite check after the division | Checked before the division (`circumcenter`); same result | ca86263b7 |
| `geo()` drops the kind (`guide/cover.rs`, `region_build.rs`, `entry/room.rs`, also `load/rings.rs`) | The kind is kept: `<STAGE>_GEOMETRY` (out of range) and new `<STAGE>_GEOMETRY_INVALID`, through `geo_refusal` | 268fa07c5 |
| The switch is read one time (`OnceLock`) | Documented in `planner_switch.rs` | c5df0afae |
| fig8 2D Pocket readings test without a light twin | Not changed: the test is in PR #4328, not merged into `side/path-kernel` | - |
| `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` | The decision file says what guards a re-record (the gate never sets it; a re-record is a diff of committed goldens that the review reads). No new mechanism | c5df0afae |
| `notes.rs` word lists, `l1_guide.rs` reasons | Not changed: they are in `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/` (owned by #4406) or test-side classifiers outside class B | - |

## Minor items

- The citations of `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md` point to `RECOMMENDED.md` (`## #4024`) in each file outside `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/` (that directory is left to #4406); `docs/decisions/4055-pathkernel-skeleton.md` points to the live record and to the new dependency facts (b0f7938a0, c5df0afae).
- `docs/decisions/4407-pathkernel-dependency-edges.md` has the facts that **No new dependency between our crates without a decision** asks for both edges: the imported items from the `use` lines, why the caller cannot pass them in, what rebuilds, and the maintainer's approval of 2026-11-25 (c5df0afae).
- New test files: `crates/pathkernel/tests/no_silent/{entry,exit}.rs` join the `laws` binary through `#[path]` lines in `laws.rs` (no new top-level binary). They are outside `laws/` because #4406 edits that directory now.

## Pins

- `camcraft-pathkernel` lib: `region_check::tests::a_loop_against_its_nesting_is_found`, `geo_tests::a_geometry_error_keeps_its_kind`.
- `camcraft-pathkernel` laws: `no_silent_entry::a_refused_try_is_named_in_the_notes_or_in_the_refusal`, `no_silent_entry::a_cut_above_the_material_top_says_why_the_asked_entry_is_not_flown`, `no_silent_exit::an_exit_with_no_room_for_its_lead_out_names_the_fallback`, `no_silent_exit::the_exit_constructors_share_one_checked_path` (with `Exit::new(None, 4.0, 5.0)` refused by `RAPID_IN_MATERIAL`).
- `camcraft-motion` lib: `kernel_emit::tests::an_exit_under_the_clearance_height_is_refused_by_name`, `kernel_emit::tests::an_exit_fallback_goes_to_the_notes`, `kernel_emit::tests::a_circle_cut_with_no_chord_above_the_tolerance_is_refused_as_empty`.
- `camcraft-motion` kernel_laws: `k3_load::a_trochoidal_pitch_above_the_limit_is_said_on_the_status_line`.
- `camcraft-geometry` lib: `geo2d::medial::tests::a_flat_or_not_finite_triangle_has_no_circumcentre` (documents the order; the result was the same before).

## Readings

No measured reading changed: the `kernel_laws` tables k3 (`READ`), k4 (`LIFTS`, `CROSSINGS`) and k6a pass unchanged, and the baselines of `pass_start_levels` (45) pass. The converter's own test plans changed their exit from 5 above the level (Z 3, under the clearance Z 10, raised in silence before) to the clearance height; the moves are the same.

## Results

Head `81a919838` (Exit::new takes the top): `cargo check --tests` and clippy `-D warnings` for pathkernel and motion: ok; pathkernel lib 7 and laws 177 pass; motion `kernel_laws` 32 and `kernel_emit` 10 pass. The results below are for the head before it.

The branch merged `origin/side/path-kernel` at `21fd9e57d` (PR #4412, class A, K-fixA). One conflict: the provenance line of `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws.rs`; the side branch's wording is kept. No law test of the new verdicts went red, so no pin was adapted.

On the final (merged) head:
- `cargo check --tests -p` geometry, pathkernel, motion: ok (app: ok on the pre-merge head; the merge touches only pathkernel tests).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings -p` geometry, pathkernel, motion: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel`: lib 7 pass, laws 177 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws`: 32 pass; `--test pass_start_levels`: 45 pass; `--lib kernel_emit`: 10 pass.

On the pre-merge head `fddbabe3b`:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel` (a full batch: the diff touches `camcraft-geometry` and two `Cargo.toml` comments): 1234 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 76.3 min.

Not run here, by the coordinator's order: the light lane and a second batch. The sync worker runs the full batch, the heavy `motion` and `app` steps and the light lane on the final tree of `side/path-kernel` right after this PR merges.

## Not exercised

- No public value reaches `NOT_ORIENTED` (see the first row); the guard is pinned on the loops.
- No fixture reaches a geometry error inside `Ctx::holds` or the air clip, a non-finite helix point, a ring piece refused for `REPEATED_START`, or `NO_END_DIRECTION`; these paths are read, not run.
- No heavy step (P2 PR). No example catalog suite: no posted toolpath changes (the kernel is behind the switch, default old).

title: test(ui): keep the grid through both origin-axes switches
body:
## What and why

Add the two missing UI regression tests from #3377. The Display-menu test stays unchanged.

- `egui_app::tests::view_names::the_browser_axes_checkbox_leaves_the_ground_grid_visible` opens the Browser View menu and clicks `Show world origin axes`.
- `egui_app::tests::display_menu::the_viewport_axes_button_leaves_the_ground_grid_visible` clicks the actual viewport navigation button at its live HUD anchor.

Each test starts with axes and Grid on. Each checks that the action hides the axes, leaves Grid on, and keeps the production `ground_grid_lines` result nonempty. No test sets the axes field directly. The tests use the existing shell harness and directory suite. No new test binary or production seam is needed.

The existing Display-menu test and reverse grid-off/axes-on coverage stay unchanged. The two touched modules contain 11 tests, up from nine. The decision is in `docs/decisions/3377-grid-axes-switch-tests.md`.

## Verification

Tested source head: `b0ea9f8bc4e1d02d578cbfefff04c2b3e21be992`.
Base: upstream `main` at `231b17d8b4ce33d9825b48c69e81952167b74c1c`.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib leaves_the_ground_grid_visible -- --nocapture`: both new tests pass.
- Negative control: temporarily restore `!state.show_world_axes || !state.show_grid` in `ground_grid_lines`. Both tests fail at their final grid-output assertion. Restore the production guard. Both tests pass again. The negative control is not in the diff.
- Display-menu module: eight tests pass. Browser view-switch module: three tests pass.
- `the_ground_grid_is_a_round_spaced_floor`: passes, including the reverse grid-hidden/axes-visible direction.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base 231b17d8b4ce33d9825b48c69e81952167b74c1c`: all 10 selected steps pass on the committed head. UI lib: 1796 passed, eight ignored. The selected integration suites pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passes on the committed head.
- `cargo xtask gate light --only 'motion light:' --only 'app light:'`: all five test-target steps pass on the committed head. This runs all 11 light twins. The broad all-app `--no-run` preparation step is excluded; each selected target builds normally.
- `git diff --check`: passes.

Linux checks use a three-job budget. The UI gate reports the software Vulkan adapter, llvmpipe.

## Scope and limits

Tests and the per-issue decision only. No production behavior, dependency, renderer, geometry, toolpath, post, simulation, collision, or numeric-policy change. No pixel golden changes. No full heavy, release, or example-catalog lane. The standalone app was not launched. No new before/after screenshots are claimed: this test-only change has no visual difference. The harness uses the real controls and production grid generator; it does not prove physical-machine safety.

The default rustfmt check reports existing formatting differences in these modules. Existing formatting is preserved outside the new tests. No broad formatting rewrite is included.

No green-CI claim is made. Required rules and actual PR checks are checked separately before handoff. This is an outside-contributor PR for manual maintainer handling, not a counted collaborator review.

Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3377#issuecomment-7226619228

No scout was commissioned. Bounded direct searches located the Browser switch, viewport dispatch and HUD anchor, existing Display tests, shell helpers, and ground-grid generator.

Changelog: none (test-only)
Effort: low

Fixes #3377

title: test(motion): fold the motion integration tests into domain directory suites
body:
## What changed

- The 153 flat, non-slow test files of `crates/motion/tests/` move into ten domain directory suites:
  - `adaptive2d` (17 modules)
  - `contour2d` (20)
  - `machining2d` (22)
  - `holes` (13)
  - `entry_links` (12)
  - `machining3d` (16)
  - `finishing3d` (13)
  - `multiaxis` (14)
  - `turning` (20)
  - `edges_edm` (6)
- Each suite has a `main.rs` that declares one module for each former file.
- The `SLOW_BINARIES` `finish3d`, `pivot5d` and `flow` stay flat binaries. Batch still skips them, and release still runs them.
- `rest_adaptive` and `rotary_flow` were directory suites before. They do not change.
- `camcraft-motion` now has 15 test binaries. Before this change it had 158.
- The files move with `git mv`. Git shows most of them as pure renames. In 14 moved files, one or two lines change:
  - Five `mod common;` lines become `use crate::common;`. The suite root declares `common` one time.
  - The three `adaptive_troch_*` files share `common/adaptive_troch.rs`. The `adaptive2d` root declares it one time as `fixtures`. Clippy `duplicate_mod` refuses three copies in one binary. Their two ignore reasons now name the `motion heavy: adaptive2d` step.
  - `arc_turn_kinds`, `adaptive_orbit_seam` and `rotary_adaptive` get a `../` prefix on one `#[path]` or `include_str!`. `tests/fixtures/` and `tests/rotary_adaptive_fixture/` stay in place, because the lib unit tests also read them.
  - Two regenerate commands in doc comments name the new suite.
- The Gate map paragraphs stay in the modules. The gate reads them through the suite root (#3186).
- xtask: two live-tree tests named old binaries. Now they name the suites that hold `arcs` (`contour2d`) and `cross_invariance` (`holes`). This is an expected change.
- `docs/MACHINE-ONBOARDING.md`: the links to moved files point to the new paths.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3189-fold-motion-suites.md`.

## Cause

Each flat file was a separate test binary. Each binary links the full crate again. The issue measured 4.03 GB for one target set (#919).

## Tests

- Pin: `motion_tests_fold_into_at_most_sixteen_binaries` (xtask, `directory_selection_tests.rs`). The pin reads the live tree. It checks that motion has at most 16 test binaries, and that each motion slow binary is still a flat file.
  - Red on unchanged upstream/main c79c9b24f: `158 motion test binaries (at most 16)`.
  - Green after the fold (15 binaries).
- Test counts, `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --tests -- --list`:
  - before: 2014 tests, 78 ignored (`--list --ignored`);
  - after: 2014 tests, 78 ignored;
  - after the refresh (head 5673a882f): 2015 tests, 78 ignored. Main added `closed_model_chamfer_preserves_circular_interpolation` to `chamfer_circular.rs`. The merge carried it to `edges_edm/chamfer_circular.rs`.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --tests` (all binaries, debug, 6 test threads): all green, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: 12 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (19.4 min). It ran the ten new suites and the xtask unit tests.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on the final head: 9 steps (release build and 8 `motion heavy:` suites), 0 failed, 0 stalled (9.0 min). `edges_edm` and `turning` have no ignored tests, so they have no heavy step.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops on `xtask/src/unit_sweep.rs:67` (`needless_bool`). This PR does not change that file; its text is the same as on upstream/main. xtask is not in the gate clippy list.

## Refresh (head 5673a882f)

- The head is a merge of upstream/main e80c70942 into the branch (a merge commit, no rebase).
- One conflict: `xtask/src/gate_maps_tests.rs`, test `moved_suites_live_in_their_owner_crate_and_not_in_app`. Main (#3188) and this branch each changed the owner rows and the source read to directory suites. The result keeps the post rows, the sim rows and the source read of main. It keeps the motion row of this branch (`contour2d`).
- Pin proof for the resolution: with the motion row of main (`arcs`), the test is red: `arcs missing from crates/motion/tests`. With `contour2d` it is green.
- `cargo check --tests -p <pkg>`, one package at a time: `xtask`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-sim`, `camcraft-tools`, `camcraft-ui-kit`, `camcraft-app`, `camcraft-ui`. All compile.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on 5673a882f: 12 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (19.1 min).
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on 5673a882f: 9 steps (release build and 8 `motion heavy:` suites), 0 failed, 0 stalled (7.5 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. The `xtask` clippy result is the same as before (`unit_sweep.rs:67`, a file of main).
- The gate results in "Tests" are from the first head 70b70c998.

## Goldens moved

None. This PR changes no generator code, and no test writes a golden. I did not run `example_catalog`: it is an app suite, and this PR does not change app or any generator.

## Not exercised

- `cargo xtask gate batch`. The issue names it in "Done means". I ran the quick tier (all ten new suites) and the motion heavy lanes. The post-merge gate runs batch on main.
- `cargo xtask gate light`. The heavy run covers the full tests of the light twins.
- Disk and build time saving: not measured on this machine.
- Wall time: some suites are now long in debug. In the quick gate (16 test threads) `adaptive2d` took 190 s, `entry_links` 167 s and `machining3d` 96 s. Batch runs suites in parallel lanes. No single test changed. The decision record says how to split a suite that proves too slow.

## Overlaps

These open PRs change files that this PR moves. They change other lines, not the same functions. Git rename detection can carry their edits to the new paths. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #4379 (`rotary.rs`)
- #4316 (`center_cut_owed.rs`)

title: feat(post): Cobra Cut D 0.25 qualities for one 40 mm Agie punch
body:
## What changed

- Two new machine conditions select two new Agie work qualities:
  - `AGIE_COBRA_RA030` requests `CCD030`: Ra 0.30, a main cut and three trims.
  - `AGIE_COBRA_RA070` requests `CCD070`: Ra 0.70, a main cut and two trims.
- `agie_setup::Quality` gets `Ccd030` and `Ccd070`. Each has its measured 40 mm offsets:
  - CCD030: 250, 170, 145 and 135 µm.
  - CCD070: 245, 165 and 140 µm.
- `Quality::wire()` gives the native wire name. The piece and each work write `ID_THREAD` from it. A Cobra job writes `Cobra Cut D 0.25` two times and no `Berco`.
- The clearance and miter checks use the rough (first) offset of the selected quality.
- The operator review names the wire, the offsets and the number of TECCUT passes.
- Refusals. No file is written for these:
  - The encoder refuses other heights with `SetupError::UnqualifiedCobraHeight`.
  - The post refuses a die opening, an open cutoff, a punch group and a DXF arc punch. The group and arc refusal now names the selected condition and its height.
- The 1 mm separation is unchanged.
- The user guide and the site page have a new Cobra Cut D section.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/2986-agie-cobra-40.md`.

## Cause

The native post knew only Berco Cut 0.25 qualities. It wrote the wire as a fixed string at piece and work level.

## Tests

Pins (both red before the fix):
- `camcraft-post` lib `agie::cobra_tests`:
  - `cobra_cut_d_sets_the_wire_and_quality_of_a_40_mm_punch`. The expected SBL is the Berco 40 mm SBL with only the quality line and the two wire values replaced.
  - `cobra_cut_d_refuses_other_heights_and_sides_without_files`
  - `the_setup_encoder_holds_cobra_cut_d_to_40_mm`
  - `cobra_cut_d_bounds_the_cut_with_its_own_rough_offset`
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native` `cobra::`. These run the CLI on the shipped examples and include a project save and load:
  - `a_cobra_condition_requests_its_quality_and_wire_on_a_40_mm_punch`
  - `a_cobra_condition_refuses_other_heights_without_a_directory`
  - `a_cobra_condition_refuses_a_group_an_arc_punch_a_die_and_a_cutoff`
  - `a_cobra_condition_with_another_wire_diameter_is_refused`. This one is a guard. It already passed before the fix, because the existing condition and tool gate refuses the mismatch.

Red before the fix:
- The post pins did not compile, because `Ccd030`, `Ccd070`, `wire()` and `UnqualifiedCobraHeight` did not exist.
- The app pins failed with `Select AGIE_QN2 (Fine Ra 0.30 µm) or AGIE_BERCO_RA035 ...`.

Mutations. Each mutation was put in, run, and restored:
1. Old `piece.rs` with the fixed Berco wire: red in the post and app wire pins.
2. Clearance with the QN2 rough offset instead of the quality's offset: `cobra_cut_d_bounds_the_cut_with_its_own_rough_offset` red.
3. The encoder maps Cobra to `UnqualifiedQualityHeight`: `the_setup_encoder_holds_cobra_cut_d_to_40_mm` red.
4. The group refusal names `AGIE_BERCO_RA035`: the app refusal pin red. This mutation survived the first version of the test, so I made the test stronger.

Gate on the final tree (`7a68cb5b3`, base `b2afd64ed`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 361 steps, 0 failed. This includes `post suites: agie_safe_setup`, `agie_inspection`, `app suites: agie_native`, `example_catalog*`, `wire_post` and `wire_post_alias`.
- After the gate, one test edit fixed a clippy finding. Then `cargo xtask gate test cobra --binary agie_native` passed (4 of 4) and `cargo xtask gate test quality --binary agie_native` passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 1 step (release build), ok. No light twin was selected.
- Heavy lanes: not run. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 75 app heavy steps. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives no heavy step to a P6 PR and no full heavy lane to any PR.
- The branch merges cleanly with the current `upstream/main` (`878f8c2f2`). That main has no change in the touched files.

## Goldens moved

None. The `example_catalog*`, `agie_native` and `agie_safe_setup` suites ran green, with all Berco goldens byte-equal. No new golden file was added. The tests derive the Cobra SBL from the Berco output.

## Not exercised

- A real or emulated Agie control import of a Cobra job. The offsets come from the two synthetic offline jobs of the issue. They are motion values, not a surface measurement.
- Te, Tkm and the three options of the request copy CCB030 (1.50, 1.00, three disabled). The issue gives no other values. See the decision file.
- No UI change. The post dialog line still names only AGIE_QN2.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes the touched Agie files.

title: feat(post): pattern folders with linear and grid copies at the post
body:
Effort: high

## What changed

This PR adds a pattern folder to the operation list. A folder holds member operations of one setup. The post writes the members again at each enabled copy of a linear or grid pattern. All copies use the WCS of the setup: the moves shift, and the work offset stays the same.

- Schema: `PatternDef` in `crates/app/src/schema.rs`. It has `setup`, `suppressed`, `order_mode` (`ByTool` is the default, or `ByPart`), `kind` (`Linear` or `Grid`), `members` and `disabled_instances`. The copy numbers start at 1. Copy 1 is where the members are now.
- Row law: a folder is a list row, the same as a Pause entry. It uses `OperationMeta::order` for its position. Its members stand directly after it, in folder order. The commands keep this order. A member moves only inside its folder.
- Commands (`crates/app/src/commands/pattern_folder.rs`): `CreatePatternFolder`, `EditPatternFolder`, `SetPatternMembers`, `SetPatternInstanceEnabled` and `DeletePatternFolder`. Delete ungroups the members. Each command is undoable.
  - `ReorderOperation` and `RenameOperation` take folders.
  - `DeleteOperation` and `DeleteEntity` remove a deleted member from its folder. Undo puts it back.
- Validation at command creation: the command checks counts (1-1000), the total copies (10000 at most), spacings (finite, above 0) and directions (finite, in XY, not zero). Grid directions must not be parallel. It also checks members: each is a milling operation, is not a probe, is in one setup, is named once and is in no other folder. Nested folders are not possible because a member must be an operation. At least one copy must stay on.
- cl: `cl::transform::copies` (`crates/cl/src/cl/transform_copies.rs`) joins the translated copies of one path. Between two copies, the link goes straight up to the clearance plane, across, then straight down. Cycle anchors and compensated spans move with their copy. Plasma and tilted moves are refused by name.
- Posting (`crates/app/src/posting_pattern.rs`):
  - `ByTool`: each member is one section over all enabled copies, so it has one `T.. M6`.
  - `ByPart`: all members cut one copy, then the next copy. The after-action and the setup-change stop go only on the last section of each operation.
  - The post refuses these cases by name: a turned or flipped WCS, a member that is missing or in another setup, and members that are not directly after the folder.
  - `viewer_map` maps every line of every copy.
  - Per-operation files refuse a `ByPart` folder by name.
- Verification gate: each shifted copy is checked against the machine travel of the setup (`MachineCheck::check_path`) and against its fixtures (`fixture_struck::op_hits`). A not-judged line names the folders whose other copies the stock sim does not judge.
- Project file: a new entity kind, `pattern`, with no version step. A document with no folder saves the same bytes as before. An older build refuses the unknown kind by name. The folder's display name is saved too.
- MCP (`crates/app/src/mcp/pattern_tools.rs`): new tools `create_pattern_folder`, `edit_pattern_folder`, `set_pattern_members`, `set_pattern_instance_enabled` and `delete_pattern_folder`. `get_job` lists `pattern_folders` only when the document has one. `rename_operation` and `reorder_operation` accept a folder.
- Docs: I regenerated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`, and I added a row to the guide table (`site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md`). The camcraft-mcp skill has new tool rows (process file).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3012-pattern-folder.md`.

Process change: yes (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`: the new MCP tool rows only).

## Review fix (head `07cd14690`)

This commit closes the findings of the review of `eaa90f1d6`.

- A pattern folder is not a model. `model::is_model` excludes it, thus `model_entities`, `get_job` and the laws that read them do not see a folder.
- The load checks the membership law over the whole file (`pattern_dto::validate_members`). It refuses a member that is not an operation row of the file. It refuses an operation that two folders name. The check runs before any world write.
- The post plan and the copy gate refuse by name an operation that two active folders name. A folder takes its members by name, not by a count of the rows that follow.
- The MCP tools refuse a `dir` entry that is not a number.

New pins, in `crates/app/tests/mcp/pattern_folder_law.rs` (`mcp` directory suite):

- `pattern_folder_law::a_folder_is_not_a_model`
- `pattern_folder_law::a_file_breaking_the_membership_law_is_refused_at_load`
- `pattern_folder_law::two_folders_that_name_one_operation_refuse_the_post_by_name`
- `pattern_folder_law::a_by_part_stop_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy`
- `pattern_folder_law::a_by_part_setup_change_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy`
- `pattern_folder_law::a_copy_that_strikes_a_fixture_blocks_the_post_until_it_is_off`
- `pattern_folder_law::a_copy_outside_the_machine_travel_blocks_the_post_until_it_is_off`

Mutation checks on this head (the guard removed, the 15 `pattern_folder*` tests run, the guard put back):

| Mutation | Red pins |
|---|---|
| `is_model` has no folder clause | `a_folder_is_not_a_model` |
| The load does not call `validate_members` | `a_file_breaking_the_membership_law_is_refused_at_load` |
| `refusal` does not check a second owner | `two_folders_that_name_one_operation_refuse_the_post_by_name` |
| The after-action goes on each by-part section (`posting.rs:1321`) | `a_by_part_stop_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy`, `a_by_part_setup_change_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy` |
| The setup change goes on each by-part section (`posting.rs:1361`) | `a_by_part_setup_change_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy` |
| `pattern_problems` judges no folder | the fixture pin, the travel pin, the two-folder pin |
| `dir` drops an entry that is not a number | `a_folder_is_not_a_model` (the `dir` assert) |
| `enabled_offsets` ignores `disabled_instances` | 5 pins, with the "copy 2 is not cut" assert of the by-tool pin |

With each guard put back, 15 of 15 tests pass.

One change has no pin of its own: the plan takes the members by name and not by count. The row-law refusal and the second-owner refusal together make the two forms give the same sections. Thus no test can see the difference.

Gate results on `07cd14690`, against `upstream/main` `4d891498e`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 1231 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (24.5 min). The `cl` change makes the quick tier fall back to the batch plan. The run includes `clippy -D warnings`, `app suites: mcp`, and `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 of 6 steps pass (9.3 min).

No golden changed in this commit.

## Tests

The results below are from the first head (`eaa90f1d6`). The section "Review fix" has the results of the final head.

These pins are in the `mcp` directory suite (`crates/app/tests/mcp/pattern_folder.rs`, `pattern_folder_post.rs`) and in the cl unit tests:

- `pattern_folder::a_folder_is_created_reordered_renamed_and_undone`
- `pattern_folder::edits_members_copies_and_delete_are_undoable`
- `pattern_folder::bad_patterns_and_members_are_refused_when_the_command_is_made`
- `pattern_folder::folders_round_trip_and_documents_without_them_write_no_key`
- `pattern_folder_post::by_tool_posts_each_member_once_over_every_enabled_copy`: linear, copy 2 off, golden. The tool changes are the same as the program without the folder.
- `pattern_folder_post::by_part_posts_every_member_at_one_copy_then_the_next`: grid, copy 4 off, golden, and the per-op refusal.
- `pattern_folder_post::a_folder_the_post_cannot_write_refuses_by_name`: out-of-block member order, turned WCS.
- `pattern_folder_post::mcp_tools_create_edit_reorder_undo_save_and_open_a_folder`
- `cl::transform::copies::tests::*` (6 tests)

Mutation checks (each guard file put back to `upstream/main`, then the pins run):

- `posting.rs`: the by-tool, by-part and refusal pins are red.
- `commands/operation/meta.rs`, `commands/delete_entity.rs` and `posting_per_op.rs`: the reorder, delete, rename, MCP and per-op pins are red.
- With the fix restored, all pins are green.

Gate results, against `upstream/main`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: the cl change makes the quick tier fall back to the batch tier, with 1231 steps (36.4 min).
  - 1230 steps passed. This includes every app suite and the `example_catalog*` suites.
  - The one failure was a clippy lint (`err().expect()`) in the new per-op pin. Commit `eaa90f1d6` fixes it.
  - On the final head `eaa90f1d6`, the gate's own `clippy -D warnings` step and the `app suites: mcp` step ran again. Both are green.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 of 6 steps pass (15.9 min).
- Heavy lanes: not run (see "Not exercised"). `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches 116 steps.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

There are two new goldens, made with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`. No existing golden changed.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/pattern_folder/fanuc_linear_by_tool.nc`: 3 sections and 3 tool changes. Each link between copies is one `G00` at Z25.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/pattern_folder/fanuc_grid_by_part.nc`: 7 sections. Face1 is first, then Face2 and Face3 at copies 1, 2 and 3.

The example catalog suites ran as part of the gate. They have no folder, so their output does not change.

At the start of each copy, a `G00` repeats the point where the link ended. This line comes from the face path's own first rapid. It does not move the tool.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes: I did not run them. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) says that a P6 PR gets no heavy step. `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` shows the reach.
- The stock sim and the gouge check judge each member at copy 1 only. The stock-bounds check for the copies is also not done. This work is #3013. The not-judged line says this on every surface that reports the post.
- If a setup has no machine, the travel of a shifted copy is not checked. The program's own limit check still uses the default machine.
- The link rapid between two copies (by tool) is not part of the copy gate. `pattern_problems` judges each copy alone, against the machine travel and the fixtures. The link is at the clearance height or above, and the first-rapid law refuses a clearance height below a fixture top. #3013 lists the check of each link between copies.
- The review made two optional remarks that this PR does not change: the text of `TransformError::TiltedMove` says "mirrored" for a copy, and `posting.rs` is longer than 400 lines.
- UI: the browser shows a folder as a plain row. The folder UI is #3016.
- G52 and M98 output for compact programs is #3017.
- `verification_report` translates each copy of each member when it runs. A very large pattern can make the report slow.

## Overlaps

These PRs change the same files but other functions. The PR that merges second must refresh:

- #4288: `posting.rs` (`post_serves`, `HeightRefs`) and `project/file.rs` (`ToolKindDto`).
- #4368: `schema.rs`, `delete_entity.rs`, `mcp/mod.rs` and `mcp/tools.rs` (append rows).
- #4379 and #4173: `project/file.rs`.
- #4302 and #4238: `mcp/mod.rs` and `mcp/tools.rs`.
- #4383: `lib.rs`.
- #3103: `mcp/job.rs`.

Refs #3013 (in part: the travel and fixture checks for each copy).

Changelog: Pattern folders: post member operations again at each copy of a linear or grid pattern. Cut by tool (one tool change for each operation) or by part. Each copy can be turned off. There are undoable commands, MCP tools and project save.

Fixes #3012

title: test(post,sim): fold the flat integration tests into domain directory suites
body:
## What changed

- `crates/post/tests/` had 143 flat test binaries. It now has 9 directory suites.
- `crates/sim/tests/` had 95 flat test binaries. It now has 8 directory suites.
- Each old file is a module of one suite (`tests/<suite>/<old name>.rs`). Its text did not change, except for these mechanical edits:
  - `mod recorded;` and the other shared helpers (`inverted_support`, `mirror_trace`, `macro_b`, `ac_trunnion_support`) became `use crate::<helper>;`. Each suite's `main.rs` declares a helper one time, by `#[path]`.
  - `legacy_program` (in `script_dialects`) and `coincident_arcs/reader.rs` (in `script_arcs`) are declared one time in `main.rs`. `clippy::duplicate_mod` refuses two declarations in one binary.
  - Each relative `include_str!` / `include_bytes!` and `#[path]` path gained one `../`.
  - A doc command `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test <old>` now reads `--test <suite> <old>::`.
- A submodule directory with one owner moved with its owner: `agie_safe_setup`, `fanuc_post`, `heidenhain_cycles`, `sodick_ln2w`, `upright_after_tilt`, `richauto_safety` and sim `model_excess`.
- The data directories did not move: `golden/`, `recorded/`, `klartext/`, `coincident_arcs/`. Other crates read them by path.
- `recorded::tmp` adds a per-process counter to the temp file name. One process now runs all script modules in parallel. Two modules that post the same script and case must not write the same file.
- `every_shipped_post_script_has_its_suite` now looks in `tests/script_goldens/`. It also checks that `main.rs` declares each script module.
- Six `xtask` pins named old post and sim binaries. They now name the suite that holds the module (`fanuc_post` is in `script_dialects`, and so on).
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` and `docs/tester-kits/fanuc-mgi-blank/README.md` name the new paths.

Post suites: `script_goldens`, `script_cycles`, `script_probe`, `script_wcs`, `script_rotary`, `script_edm`, `script_dialects`, `script_arcs`, `post_engine`.
Sim suites: `stock_engines`, `stock_field`, `stock_carry`, `fixture_laws`, `reach_laws`, `gouge_laws`, `rest_credit`, `sim_timeline`.

All post suite names match `OUTPUT_SUITES` in `.github/scripts/post-merge-report.sh` (`post_engine`, `script_*`). A red post suite on main is still a wrong-output failure, and that workflow script does not change.

## Cause

Each flat file in `tests/` is its own binary. Each binary links the crate and its dependencies again. Issue #919 measured about 5.2 GB of disk for each worktree for these two crates.

## Tests

- Test list, before and after (`cargo test -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim --tests -- --list`): 2353 tests before and 2353 after. A script matched each old test name to exactly one new name with a module prefix: 0 missing, 0 extra.
- `#[test]` count in the source: 1579 before (post 917, sim 662) and 1579 after.
- Binaries: 242 test targets before, 21 after (17 suites, the 2 libs, and 2 bin targets).
- Pin `recorded_streams::every_shipped_post_script_has_its_suite` (suite `script_goldens`):
  - It was red after the fold and before the fix ("has no suite .../tests/script_fanuc.rs").
  - Mutation: I removed `mod script_fanuc;` from `script_goldens/main.rs`. The pin was red. I restored the line. The pin was green.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: 31 steps, 0 failed (post lib, the 9 post suites, the 8 sim suites, xtask unit tests). An earlier run on the first commit also ran about 70 app suites for a `crates/post/src` comment: all green; that comment is no longer in the diff.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p xtask`: 365 passed, 0 failed (with the asset and gate-map tests).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` stops on `xtask/src/unit_sweep.rs:67` (`if` guard returns a bool literal). This PR does not touch that file. The same error is on `upstream/main`.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`): 6 steps, 0 failed.
- Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` plans 0 steps. The heavy lanes cover only `HEAVY_CRATES` (kernel, motion, app). The 5 `#[ignore]`d heavy tests of sim had no heavy step before this PR, and they have none after; that is not a change. They are still in their suites (`stock_field`, `fixture_laws`, `rest_credit`) and `cargo test -- --list` lists them.

## Goldens moved

None. No post script, machine file or generator changed. The fold moves test sources only. The goldens and recorded streams stay at their paths, and every golden test ran green in the quick gate. I did not run the `example_catalog` suites: no post or toolpath output changed.

## Not exercised

- The `recorded::tmp` counter has no test of its own. A race between two modules with one tag is not deterministic, so a test cannot make it fail every time.
- The release tier was not run. The 5 heavy-lane sim tests (`#[ignore]`d) are still in the suites. The heavy plan finds them (see above).
- Windows and macOS were not built. The change is paths in Rust source with `/`, which all three hosts read.

## Overlaps

These open PRs edit files that this PR moves. Git applies their edits to the renamed files when they merge main. A PR that adds a new flat file must move it into a suite:
- #4395 (`script_heidenhain_klartext.rs`, `klartext/`).
- #4387 (`script_heidenhain.rs`).
- #4380 (`recorded/mod.rs`, different function).
- #4371 (`setup_change.rs`, `upright_after_tilt.rs` and their directories).
- #4298 (`tormach_lathe_post.rs`, `tormach_plasma_post.rs`).
- #4009 (sim `undercut_laws.rs`, `verify_avoid_undercut.rs`).
- #2646 (adds `script_hurco_winmax.rs` and other new post files). `every_shipped_post_script_has_its_suite` will ask for `script_goldens/script_hurco_winmax.rs`.

Whichever merges second refreshes.

title: fix(post): the Mazak preamble states G94
body:
## What changed

The Mazak post wrote every F word as a feed per minute, but it never wrote `G94`. A control in `G95` (from its power-on setting, an earlier program or MDI) reads `F1200` as 1200 mm per revolution.

Each section preamble of `assets/posts/mazak.cps` now writes `G94` with its other modal words:

```
G17 G90 G94 G54 G40 G49 G80
```

This is the block that the Haas post writes. #4150 (PR #4169) did the same for the Sinumerik 840D preamble. Each section restates `G94`, so a restart at a later section also gets it. The decision file `docs/decisions/4343-mazak-g94.md` records the dropped option (`G94` once in `onOpen`).

## Goldens moved

29 Mazak goldens. Each changes in its preamble line only (`G17 G90 G5x` to `G17 G90 G94 G5x`):

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/mazak/*.nc` (17), `golden/nc/inch/mazak/*.nc` (2) and `golden/nc/synth_mazak.nc`;

In `golden/explain/mazak.nc` the preamble comment now reads `(XY PLANE, ABSOLUTE POSITIONS, FEED PER MINUTE)`. The post's `commentMax` of 60 keeps whole meanings only, so "WORK OFFSET 1" no longer fits. The Haas explain golden ends the same way for the same block.

## What changed

- A new catalog case `examples/catalog/3d/rest`. It follows `examples/catalog/README.md`: `model/` with its generator, `build.camscript`, `rest.camproj`, `rest.nc`, `case.toml` and `README.md`.
- The part is original: a 60 x 50 x 4 mm plate with two 13 x 30 x 10 mm ribs. The channel between the ribs is 8 mm wide. The walls are vertical.
- Operation 1: a 3D Pocket with a 12 mm end mill (`EM-1200-2FL`). It cannot go into the channel below the rib tops.
- Operation 2: a 3D Pocket with a 6 mm end mill (`EM-0600-4FL`). The re-machining mask (the stock of the program ahead) limits it. It cuts only the channel. The rib ends are convex, so no rest material stands at the two mouths. The 6 mm tool enters there through space that the 12 mm tool cleared.
- The README shows the rest region as a top view with coordinates. It names the NC lines to look at.
- `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/case_3d_rest.rs`: the two case tests (`regenerates`, `rebuilds`) and a pin on the rest region.

- `docs/decisions/2867-3d-rest-case.md`: what was chosen and dropped.

No product code changed.

## Cause

The catalog had no rest-machining case for 3D (#2392). An earlier note on #2867 said that no 3D operation has a rest input. The 3D Pocket reads the stock of the program ahead (M3.1 D). That is rest machining from the previous operations, so the case needs no new code.

Pins:
