title: feat(post): Heidenhain DIN/ISO writes the G62 filter mode and checks the T range
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps` writes the smoothing ask as `G62 T<tol> P01 <0|1> P02 0`. `P01 0` is finish and `P01 1` is rough, from `PARAM SmoothingMode`. `P02 0` is the value that the control inserts for a `G62` with T only.
- The dialect resolver has two new flags (`crates/post/src/post/heidenhain_profiles.rs`):
  - `g62_mode` (`no` / `yes` / `option2`): the control takes `P01`. On the iTNC 530 340 49x and 606 42x, `P01` needs software option 2 (HSC machining). The post writes it only when the machine file lists option 2.
  - `g62_t_max_um`: the largest documented T for each control and NC software (10 mm or 99999.999 mm; 0 = no cycle 32). Where a manual states no range, the post uses 10 mm, the narrowest documented range.
- The post refuses by name:
  - a T above the range of the control;
  - a positive T that rounds to `T0` (the control reads T 0 as the tolerance of the machine builder);
  - smoothing on a stated control without cycle 32 (TNC 410).
- Where `P01` is not written and the ask is rough, the post writes T only and gives a counted warning.
- A machine with no controller identity keeps the TNC 640 34059x-07 level of this post: `P01` is written.
- The sources and the dropped options are in `docs/decisions/4226-g62-smoothing.md`.

## Fehlmann Picomax 55 (iTNC 530, NC 340490-03)

The output is byte-identical: `G62 T<tol>`. The machine file lists no installed options, and the iTNC 530 340 49x-03 ISO manual permits `P01`/`P02` only with option 2. The research does not prove that the current output is wrong for this control. New on this machine: a rough ask gives a warning, and a T above 10 mm is refused.

## What posts now (examples)

| Machine | Ask | Block |
|---|---|---|
| no controller identity, or TNC 640 340595-08 | 0.02 mm finish | `G62 T0.02 P01 0 P02 0` |
| same | 0.1 mm rough | `G62 T0.1 P01 1 P02 0` |
| Picomax 55 (no options listed) | 0.02 mm finish or rough | `G62 T0.02` (rough: warning) |
| iTNC 530 340490-03 with option 2 listed | 0.1 mm rough | `G62 T0.1 P01 1 P02 0` |
| TNC 430 280476-01 | 0.1 mm rough | `G62 T0.1` (warning) |
| TNC 640 340595-08 | 10.001 mm | refused: `smoothing tolerance T10.001 mm is above the largest T of TNC 640 NC 340595-08 (profile tnc640-c) (10 mm)` |
| TNC 410 286060-01 | 0.02 mm | refused: `has no tolerance cycle (cycle 32 / G62)` |

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-post` `script_heidenhain`:
  - `picomax::g62::picomax_g62_stays_t_only_without_option_2`
  - `picomax::g62::g62_writes_the_finish_or_rough_mode_where_the_control_takes_it`
  - `picomax::g62::g62_refuses_a_t_outside_the_documented_range_by_name`
- `camcraft-post` lib: `post::heidenhain_dialect::tests::g62_mode_and_t_range_boundaries`, and the updated `the_picomax_control_is_the_itnc_49x_profile` and `the_script_value_names_the_flags_or_the_refusal`.
- `camcraft-app` `smoothing`: `each_dialect_writes_its_words_and_undoes_them_at_the_section_end` now asserts `P01 0` / `P01 1` for Heidenhain. `off_is_byte_identical_and_writes_no_smoothing_word` holds: a program with no smoothing posts as before.
- No recorded golden carries smoothing, so no golden changed.

## Gate results

Head `85137b87a`, merged with `origin/main` `2f766c307` for the runs.

- winbuild lane (`camcraft-post`, trial-merge head `2173bc0db`), log `gate-4226-85137b8-post.log`:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-post --lib heidenhain`: 14 passed.
  - `script_heidenhain` 19 passed, `heidenhain_cycles` 24, `heidenhain_arc_centre` 2, `heidenhain_block_form` 6, `script_heidenhain_klartext` 29.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Mac lane (`--needs app --pool`, head `85137b87a`), log `gate-4226-85137b8-app.log`:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 299 steps, 299 ok, 0 failed. The plan includes `post lib`, the `script_heidenhain` and `script_heidenhain_klartext` post suites, and the app suites `smoothing` and `example_catalog`.
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog --test example_catalog_adaptive --test example_catalog_edge_work`: all pass.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): not run. The Mac lane was in use by other workers. The reviewer runs it.

## Not exercised

- No program ran on a real control. The option 2 rule for the Picomax comes from the manual only.
- The Klartext post (`heidenhain-klartext.cps`) still refuses smoothing. `CYCL DEF 32.2 HSC-MODE` can use the same flag later.

## Merge note

The resolver file `heidenhain_profiles.rs` gets two new fields in `Flags` and split rows (iTNC 530 34049x, TNC 320 77185x, TNC 620 81760x, TNC 640 34059x-07..09). A parallel PR that adds a flag to `Flags` will touch the same struct and the Picomax test literal.

Changelog: Heidenhain DIN/ISO post: G62 now writes the finish or rough filter mode (P01) where the control takes it, and refuses a tolerance T outside the documented range of the control.

Effort: high

Fixes #4226

title: fix(drilling): Break-through follow-ups - the note, an idle selector, a full-diameter post case
body:
## What changed

This PR does the five items of #2528 (follow-ups of #2504).

1. **The Break-through note agrees with the field.** A Drill measured from its full diameter said "through holes run 2.803 mm past the part bottom (Break-through)" for a 1 mm Break-through. The note now says "through holes run 2.803 mm past the part bottom (Break-through 1.000 mm from the full diameter, plus the 1.803 mm drill point), the deepest to Z-2.803". `break_through::Broke` carries the point length (`with_point`). The Tip case, Bore and Thread keep "(Break-through)". The words "run X past the part bottom" stay, so readers of the note keep working.
2. **The "Break-through from" selector is disabled where it has no effect.** `holes_page::break_through_from_idle` gives the reason, in the generator's order:
   - a lathe's axial drill (it always measures to the tip);
   - a stated Bottom;
   - no through hole in the list;
   - a Spot, Tap, Floating tap or Ream cycle;
   - a tool with no point cone for this cycle (review fix, commit 15626f333). The page asks the generator's own rule, `drilling::through_tip_run` from the full diameter with no allowance, for the selected tool. A zero point disables the choice: for example Auto with a tap, a boring bar or an end mill, or a 180 degree drill. An unknown tool or a refused tip angle keeps the choice live.

   The combo is disabled. The reason shows when the user hovers the row (`on_disabled_hover_text`, the pattern of `fixture_menu.rs` and `feeds_page.rs`). A disabled widget shows no plain hover text, so the normal hint is used only while the row is enabled. I chose "disable" over "hide": a hidden row reads as a missing feature.
3. **A correction to the #2441 decision entry.** Issue branches do not edit `RECOMMENDED.md`, so `docs/decisions/2528-drill-point-followups.md` records the correction:
   - PR #2504 did not keep the examples byte-identical. It rebuilt the catalog case `2d/first-part` (`G73 ... Z-1. Q18.` to `G83 ... Z-2.803 Q6.`) and `examples/first-router-part.camproj` (v62 to v68, `full_diameter`, depth -1.0 to -2.802582). Only `examples/first-part.camproj` stayed the same.
   - An MCP or script patch does not default to `FullDiameter`. `add_operation` starts from the seed (`FullDiameter`). `edit_operation` applies a JSON merge patch over the stored parameters, so an omitted `break_through_from` keeps the stored value.
4. **Three file splits, structure only.** The `#[test]` counts do not change (app lib 322, motion lib 777 before item 1).
   - `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` (469 lines): the program plan moves to `stock_sim_plan.rs` (225 + 256 lines).
   - `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs` (409 lines): `PlayIndex` and `PlaySeed` move to `stock_play_index.rs` (330 + 93 lines). Their fields become `pub(super)`, because `FieldPlay` and `stock_play_head` read them.
   - `crates/motion/src/drilling/tests.rs` (508 lines): the five recognition tests move to `tests_recognize.rs` (404 + 110 lines). The shared helpers stay, so the other test modules keep their imports.
5. **Every post records a full-diameter through hole.** A new recorded stream `drill_full_diameter` (one 10 mm through hole, the default Full diameter, tip at Z-12.803) joins `recorded::CASES` and the `post_suite!` macro. Its generator guard is `recorded_post_streams::drill_full_diameter_stream_is_current`. The 15 mill posts record a program with `Z-12.803`. LinuxCNC and Heidenhain Klartext refuse the machine-less case by name, as they refuse `drill_retract`. Review fix (commit 2acc52c3e): LinuxCNC also posts the case on `assets/machines/vmc.mch`, and the NC golden `linuxcnc/drill_full_diameter_on_machine.nc` records `G73 X20 Y10 Z-12.803 R1 Q4 F60`. The guard `recorded_streams::each_drilling_post_records_the_full_diameter_depth` requires an NC golden with 12.803 from each post with a mill drilling cycle. Klartext is a named gap (`recorded::DRILL_DEPTH_GAP`): it refuses a tool with no stated kind, and the stream states none. Follow-up: #4461. The lathe, wire, sinker, plasma and waterjet posts keep their named refusals.

## Goldens moved

None. Item 5 adds 28 new goldens and one stream: the 27 `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/<post>/drill_full_diameter.{nc,refusal}` and `linuxcnc/drill_full_diameter_on_machine.nc`. No existing `.nc` golden changes. After the merge of #4382, the new goldens `fanuc/drill_full_diameter.nc` and `doosan-dnm/drill_full_diameter.nc` were written again with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`; only their preamble line changed (`G17` and `G94`).

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib: `break_through::tests::a_full_diameter_drill_names_the_field_and_its_point`.
- `camcraft-app` `break_through`: `the_default_is_today_s_millimetre_and_is_said` (the note names 1.000 mm and the 1.803 mm point for the Full-diameter drill, and "(Break-through)" for Tip and Bore).

title: fix(multiaxis): the banded parallel retip read agrees with the envelope law on slanted skins
body:
## What the feature brings (#2774, brought to the current main)

A rotary operation may state its heights as radii about the fitted
rotation axis: `RadialHeight { source, offset }` - the stock OD, the
model's max radius, or an absolute radius - as `clearance_r`,
`retract_r`, `top_r`, `bottom_r` on Rotary Contour and Rotary Parallel
and `clearance_r` + `top_r` on Rotary Offset. `None` on every field
keeps the Z-plane law byte for byte; the `*_z` fields stay.

- Heights as radii: one resolver (`app::operation::radial_heights`)
  fits the same axis the generators pose about; the radial gate
  refuses, at create/edit/retype, a clearance or retract radius that
  stands inside the work or a band that crosses.
- Band windowing: Rotary Contour keeps whole rings by tip radius
  (`band_select`); Rotary Parallel trims each skin-following pass at
  the band edges (`band_trim`); Rotary Offset caps its rho ladder at
  the bottom radius. A band that crosses no part skin refuses by name
  at the generate.
- Wrap hand-off: a band whose cylinders cover the path's whole radial
  reach hands the base path on unchanged (commit 815075be7).
- Project ladder v84 -> v85: the radii are serde-default fields, a v84
  file steps up unchanged, and a v84 reader refuses a v85 file rather
  than drop the stated radii. The three held commits (9a4da2e5f,
  8f6e59d1e, 815075be7) are cherry-picked; the two obsolete v74
  commits of the held branch are dropped and their content redone as
  the current next rung.

## The #3490 diagnosis: the two reads, what disagreed

The verdict the branch could not shake:
`Envelope { at: 38, gouge_mm: 1.544, rest_mm: 0.096 }` on a radial
band 4.0..5.5 over the r6/r5 stepped bar - the post refused a legal
program.

Both reads were re-read side by side:

- The RETIP READ the band uses, `hypot(y, z + r) - r`, is the ball
  center's radius about the axis minus the ball - the emitted tip's
  radius under the radial pose. Instrumented against the verifier it
  is exact on every kept cut move: the pose on cuts is the radial
  (lead/lag 0), so the emitted tip and the read agree.
- The ENVELOPE LAW (`stock_sim::facet_gouge`) reconstructs each ball
  center exactly (tip lifted along the pose it holds) and measures
  the exact distance of each model triangle to it. It is untouched.

What disagreed was neither read: the band trim's kept-stretch join
GLUED touching spans by extending the previous output move's end -
two arc-fit chords of a run became one straight chord. On the
raster's wrap chains (the arc around the cone's edge, ball centers on
the radius-8.5 ring) the glued chord dips 1.46 mm below the arc the
base plan rode; the reconstructed ball there stands 1.4554 mm from
the cone facet - the 1.5446 mm gouge, move for move. The verifier was
right; the kept geometry was corrupted.

## The fix

Touching spans stay consecutive Feed records (`radial_band.rs`). The
relink already reads consecutive non-lift Feeds as one run, so the
spans keep one cut - never a link between them - and the run's
polyline survives with every corner. The envelope law is untouched.

## Pins

- `rotary_verify::the_stated_radial_heights_move_the_generated_path`:
  red at the held branch with the reported verdict, green here.
- The correct-refusal side stands: a band that crosses no part skin
  refuses by name at the generate
  (`a_band_that_crosses_no_skin_is_refused_by_name`,
  `a_parallel_band_that_crosses_no_skin_is_refused_by_name`), and a
  gouging path still blocks the post.
- Motion band tests: `the_parallel_band_cuts_between_two_cylinders`,
  `a_band_that_wraps_the_whole_skin_adds_no_links`.

## Gates

- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion`: 161 suites, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim`: 98 suites, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app`: 84 suites, 0 failed (incl. the lib
  suite, the v85 round trip and the project-version suites).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1764 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui
  --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

A real machine run. The banded parallel's posted G-code is pinned by
the document-level test only (the verifier's own envelope law); no
cut was made on steel.

Unblocks #2774: with the retip read and the envelope law agreeing,
the held feature's last blocker is gone.

Changelog: Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset read
their heights as radii about the fitted axis and window their cut
band by radii; a wrapping band no longer chops its passes; banded
parallel paths verify clean on slanted skins.

Fixes #3490



## Screenshots (the review's evidence, item 9)

The Heights tab and the viewport, before and after the feature - the
same turned bar, stock, tool and operation on both sides, captured
off-screen through the guide-images harness (page and viewport crops):

Before (the Z planes only, no radial rows, no rings):

- Page: https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/raw/pr-screenshots/issue-3490/rotary-radial-before-page.png
- Viewport: https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/raw/pr-screenshots/issue-3490/rotary-radial-before-viewport.png

After (the radial rows checked with their echoes, and the two rings
about the judged axis):

- Page: https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/raw/pr-screenshots/issue-3490/rotary-radial-after-page.png
- Viewport: https://github.com/FlamingFireCoding/Camcraft/raw/pr-screenshots/issue-3490/rotary-radial-after-viewport.png

## Review rework (the nine requested findings)

Fixed on the branch in four commits; the review's own probes are
reproduced as tests:

1. Tip-to-center conversion (commit 167249f6b): the contour's radial
   relink now applies ONE tip-to-center conversion to every link (the
   ball center stands one ball radius outside the stated radius, the
   parallel twin's own law), so the posed tip stands AT the stated
   radius. Pinned by
   	he_stated_radii_are_the_tips_radii_on_every_link and the
   reviewer's app probe as
   	he_stated_contour_radii_clear_the_work (stated R8/R6.5 on the
   d12.4 bar verifies silent; it read Envelope { gouge_mm: 2.5 }
   before).
2. One-sided radial bands (commit 167249f6b):  and_window honors a
   Bottom radius alone (floor cylinder out to the skin's end) and a Top
   radius alone (axis out to the ceiling), for all three rotary kinds.
   Pinned by ^G_bottom_only_band_windows_the_parallel_passes,
   ^G_top_only_band_windows_the_parallel_passes,
   ^G_bottom_only_contour_band_windows_its_rings and the direct
   adial_band_tests.rs band-window pins.
3. Inclusive band edges (commit 167249f6b): each_band_span keeps
   constant and tangent spans with one closed-interval rule, so a span
   ON a band cylinder keeps both exact edges. The review's probe
   (constant span on the bottom cylinder beside a trimming span) is
   pinned in adial_band_tests.rs
   (^G_constant_span_on_the_bottom_cylinder_is_kept_to_its_end), with
   the start-edge, tangent, mixed enter/leave and whole-band pins
   beside it.
4. The selected rotary axis (commit 1009ddeb9): adial_context
   resolves the radii about the SAME axis generation turns about (the
   stated axis judged by ^Gxis_stated::judged_any, the free fit only
   when nothing is stated). The display cache keys the axis statement,
   the machine's work-turning rotary lines and the work offset origin.
   Pinned by ^G_stated_axis_resolves_the_radii_generation_judges (the
   R5 sphere fixture) and
   	he_radial_axis_cache_follows_a_new_axis_statement.
5. Radial input validation (commit 1009ddeb9): every set radial field is
   validated before storage - RadialHeight::is_sane keeps a finite
   offset and an absolute radius never under the axis, OpParams::is_sane
   checks each set field, and adial_gate surfaces the resolution
   failures it used to discard, with the range and ordering laws. The
   same door runs on create, edit, paste and retype. Pinned by
   ^G_radial_radius_that_is_no_radius_is_refused_at_the_command and
   ^G_radial_radius_its_source_cannot_answer_is_refused_by_name.
6. Radial overlay basis (commit 8fa787d07): the ring's second
   perpendicular is the unit dir x u (one orthonormal basis), never
   re-perpendicularized through off_axis. The plane and radius of
   every generated ring point are pinned for X, Y, Z and an oblique
   axis, and end to end through the overlay
   (	he_overlay_rings_stand_in_planes_about_the_judged_axis).
7. Valid zero-radius display (commit 8fa787d07): the echo displays the
   resolved zero for the field that permits it. The page test
   	he_default_bottom_radius_echoes_its_valid_zero drives the check
   row the way a user's click lands.
8. Project-format rollout (commit 1db582e7f): the committed example is
   regenerated by the suite's own WRITE_GOLDEN path; the diff is the
   version number and the operation stamp, and the committed .nc posts
   unchanged. See "Goldens moved" below. The compatibility break is
   declared with a BREAKING CHANGE: footer on that commit, and the
   decision entry identifies the current v85 step.
9. UI screenshots (this body): captured off-screen through the
   guide-images harness in detached worktrees, at the PR's base commit
   (before) and the rework head (after); the capture tests were
   uncommitted and deleted. The PNGs live only on the fork's
   pr-screenshots branch.

## Goldens moved

examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj: version 84 -> 85 and the
operation stamp refresh - no stored parameter, setup, machine or program
statement moved. examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc: unchanged
(the loaded project posts it move for move).

title: fix(post): retract Z before a later tool change's G49 (mazak, fanuc, doosan)
body:
## What changed

- The Mazak, Fanuc and Doosan DNM posts now lift Z before the preamble of each section after the first.
- The lift uses the `safeRetract` method of the post: `G91 G28 Z0` (default) or `G53 G00 Z<safeRetractZ>`.
- The lift comes immediately before the `G90 ... G49 G80` block. The `G90` of that block ends the `G91` of the `G28` lift. `T M6` and `G43 H` follow as before.
- The first section gets no lift. Single-tool programs do not change.
- A Go home or a setup-change lift already raises Z. The post then writes no second lift (`zUp` flag).
- Fanuc and Doosan: a tilted section leaves `G43.4` armed until the next `G49`. The post then writes `G49` before the lift, in the same order as its Go home. The upright return after a tilt (#3466) no longer writes its own lift.

## Cause

Each later preamble wrote `G49` and `T M6` at the clearance height of the previous operation. The Mazak EIA/ISO manual says that `G49` moves the axis to remove the length offset. Z could move down by the tool length, near the part. The `safeRetract` option text says "Z retract command before tool changes and at program end", but the post wrote it only at program end and on Go home.

Fanuc and Doosan had the same order. A FANUC-family control can move Z on a `G49` block with no axis word. The issue asks to fix the two posts or to record them as not affected. This PR fixes them.

## Tests

Pinning tests (new):
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_a_second_tool_g28`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_a_second_tool_g53`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_the_same_tool_called_again`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::a_trip_home_is_not_followed_by_a_second_retract`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::a_setup_change_stop_is_not_followed_by_a_second_retract`
- `upright_after_tilt::tool_change_retract::fanuc_and_doosan_cancel_tcpm_before_the_tool_change_retract`

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code, the three `retract_z_before` pins fail with `left: 0, right: 1` (no Z retract before the second G49).

Mutation results (each reverted, run, restored):
- `mazak.cps` from upstream: the three `retract_z_before` pins are red.
- `fanuc.cps` from upstream: the three pins are red.
- `doosan-dnm.cps` from upstream: the three pins are red.
- The `!zUp` guard removed (Doosan): `a_trip_home_...` and `a_setup_change_stop_...` are red (two retracts).
- The `tcpmLeft` G49 removed (Fanuc): `fanuc_and_doosan_cancel_tcpm_before_the_tool_change_retract` is red.

Gates on the final head `ce23fdaa8` (base `a5e993538`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base a5e993538`: 149 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `app suites: example_catalog`, `first_part_programs`, `program_entry`, `thread_boss`, `thread_mill`: pass.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- Targeted heavy step (P1 under the safety floor): `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: example_catalog"`: 1 step, 0 failed.
- Upstream main moved to `a721fd4dc` during the work. It changed `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` and `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs`. `git merge-tree` merges clean. Upstream's `conformance` passes on this fix (7 passed). The `comment_escape` change only replaces a fixed post count.

## Goldens moved

Each change is one `G91 G28 Z0` line before a later preamble of a multi-tool Fanuc program. The default post is Fanuc. No Mazak or Doosan golden has two tools.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/program_entry/fanuc_pause_home.nc` (+1)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.nc` (+1)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.nc` (+1)
- `examples/first-part.nc` (+2), regenerated with `camcraft-cli process`
- `examples/catalog/2d/adaptive-pocket/adaptive-pocket.nc` (+1)
- `examples/catalog/2d/edge-work/edge-work.nc` (+3)
- `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc` (+2)
- `examples/catalog/2d/hole-work/hole-work.nc` (+4)
- `examples/catalog/2d/slots/slots.nc` (+1)
- `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.nc` (+2)
- `examples/catalog/probing/probe-face/probe-face.nc` (+1)
- `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.nc`: after each tilted section the order is now `G49`, `G91 G28 Z0`, then `G90 G54 G40 G49 G80`. Before, it was `G90 G54 G40 G49 G80`, `G91 G28 Z0`, `G90`. Z is up before the preamble, and TCPM is off before the `G28`.

The catalog was regenerated with `cargo xtask catalog`. That command also rewrote the `.camproj` files: a project `version` 83 to 84, and float digits in the last place. These changes are not from this fix and are not in this PR.

`crates/app/tests/program_entry.rs`: `z_homes` counts trip homes. It no longer counts the new lift immediately before a preamble `G49` line. The tests keep their intent: one trailing home, and the mid home plus the close home.

## Not exercised

- No run on a Mazak, Fanuc or Doosan control.
- After a tilted section, the post writes `G49` before the lift, as its Go home did before. On a control where `G49` alone moves Z, that `G49` still runs before the lift. It runs in the same place as before this PR, so it is not new. A reference return under TCPM can alarm, so the post does not lift first.
- Haas, Tormach and LinuxCNC also write `G49` in each section preamble. They are out of the scope of this issue. A follow-up issue asks for the same check.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes `assets/posts/mazak.cps`, `fanuc.cps` or `doosan-dnm.cps`.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/4341-mazak-retract-before-toolchange.md`.
Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4341#issuecomment-7218043395

Effort: high

Changelog: The Mazak, Fanuc and Doosan DNM posts lift Z by the safe retract method before each later tool change, so the G49 of the next preamble never runs at the clearance height of the previous operation.

Fixes #4341

title: feat(mcp): show SolidCraft face names and re-import changes
body:
Stacked on #4364 (#4212). This PR depends on #4364: it reads the source face record that #4364 adds. This PR is opened against `main`, so its diff also shows the commits of that PR until it merges.

## Build status

- The commits of this PR were built and tested on the earlier base `773736856`. "Tests" below gives those runs.
- Then they were rebased onto `main` `a721fd4dc` and the stacked PR, with no local build. The rebase had no conflicts. The code diff did not change: the patch-ids are the same.
- This head was not built or tested locally. The maintainer's runners test it.

## What changed

This PR adds two optional parts to MCP answers. No existing key changes. A model that has no SolidCraft names gives the same answers as before.

### 1. SolidCraft face names

When a model has the source face record of a `.sc` import (#4212), these rows get new keys:

- each face row and each patch row of `list_features`;
- each face pick and each patch pick that `picks_view` shows. This one hook serves `get_operation_geometry`, `set_operation_geometry`, `get_selection`, the area and "Do not touch" views, and `pick_in_box`.

The keys:

- `source_name`: the SolidCraft name, when the face has one name.
- `source_names`: the names, sorted, when the face or the patch has more than one name.
- `source_unverified: true`: SolidCraft did not verify one of the names.

A row gets no new key in these cases:

- the model has no record;
- the record does not tile the facets of the model;
- the pick is not in the model now;
- the name is blank.

The code never shows a wrong name set or a partial name set. Chains get no names (#4215).

### 2. `changes` in the `import_model` answer for an update

When `import_model` updates a model that was in the document before the call, the answer gets this key:

```text
"changes": {
  "faces":   { "carried": N, "added": N, "missing": N },
  "patches": { "carried": N, "added": N, "missing": N },
  "chains":  { "carried": N, "added": N, "missing": N },
  "summary": "the phrase that the window shows after a re-import"
}
```

- The counts come from `revision::changes`. The window gets the same diff from `UpdateModel::changes`.
- `summary` is `FeatureChanges::describe`.
- A first import gets no `changes`. A refused import gets no `changes`.
- This is the change summary that #3814 asks for. It is one of the five scope items of #3814.

### Where the code is

- `crates/geometry/src/geometry/source_names.rs` (new, 264 lines): the name set of a face id or of a patch. It is pure code and has 7 unit tests.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/source_names.rs` (new, 157 lines): it finds the record, builds the features and writes the keys.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/reimport_changes.rs` (new, 81 lines): it keeps the models before the import and adds `changes` after the import.
- The hooks: 4 lines in `mcp/tools.rs::import_model`, 3 lines in `mcp/features.rs::list_features`, 2 lines in `mcp/pick.rs::picks_view`, and the `mod` lines.
- `mcp/tools.rs` (444 lines on `main`, 448 after this PR) and `mcp/features.rs` (435 lines, 438 after) had more than 400 lines before this PR. This PR adds only the hook lines to them. The logic is in the new files.
- `script/api.rs` does not change. #4212 and #4213 change `v_import`, so this PR does not touch that function. Thus a `cam.import` script does not get `changes`.
- The name code builds the features from the model's own facets (`features_of_facets`). The feature caches use the content as the key, not the facet order. A cached `Features` can have a different facet order, and then each facet index points to a different facet.
- No tool description changes. `mcp_doc_drift` passed on the earlier base.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/4214-mcp-face-names.md`.

### Commits

The first 5 commits are the commits of #4364. They go out of this diff when it merges. The commits of this PR:

1. `feat(mcp): import_model answers an update with its feature changes`
2. `feat(mcp): show SolidCraft face names on features and picks`
3. `test(mcp): a face pick on the .sc fixture shows its name`
4. `test(mcp): fix the .sc pick test's pocket heights`
5. `fix(mcp): name the snapshot type of reimport_changes::Before`
6. `docs(decisions): file the PR's decisions under #4214`

Commits 4 and 5 are the fixes that the build on the earlier base found: a test setup and a clippy `type_complexity` error.

New in `crates/app/tests/mcp/source_names.rs`:

- `a_face_over_two_record_faces_lists_both_and_flags_an_unverified_one`

New in `crates/app/tests/mcp/reimport_changes.rs`:

- `a_first_import_answers_with_no_changes`
- `an_update_counts_what_moved_in_each_domain`
- `the_same_file_again_carries_every_id`
- `a_refused_update_answers_with_no_changes`

`a_sc_import_names_every_face_and_patch` imports `testdata/models/hole_on_pocket_wall.sc` through the real import. Each face row and each patch row has a name. A face pick in `get_operation_geometry` shows the same keys as its `list_features` row.

Results on the earlier base `773736856`, with the stacked PR's commits of that time:

- All 17 tests of this PR: pass.
- The app lib and the 167 app test binaries that `quick` maps to this diff: pass (1,372 tests, 0 failures).
- All 39 geometry test binaries: pass (440 tests).
- The clippy step of the batch tier (`-D warnings`, all gate crates) and the kernel: pass.
- `mcp_doc_drift` and `mcp_pick`: pass.

## Not exercised

- **This head.** It was not built or tested locally (see "Build status").
- **The full batch tier.** The diff touches `crates/geometry/`, so `quick` becomes `batch`. Batch needs more disk than the build machine has. The runs above are the replacement.
- The light lane.
- `cargo fmt --check`. On the build machine it fails for `camcraft-app` with "os error 206": the command line is too long. The repository has no `rustfmt.toml`. The new files use 120 columns, as the code around them.

- The cost of the names on a large `.sc` model. The names build the features from the facets for each call, with no cache. A model without a record does no extra work.

## Open points for the maintainer

- **Fit with #3814.** The triage note on #4214 asks for your answer. This PR gives the counts that #3814 asks for, and `summary` in addition. It does not do the other four scope items of #3814. If you want #3814 separate, the commits for `changes` (1 and 5) can go as a PR of their own, with no dependency on #4364.

title: fix(recognize): read a slot with holes through or tangent to its floor
body:
## What changed

`detect_pockets` returned no feature for the reported slot (p01-flange). This PR finds two causes and fixes both, in `crates/app/src/recognize`:

1. **A hole tangent to the slot wall.** The through holes at x 39..45 touch the slot wall at x 45. So the hole ring and the outer ring of the floor share one vertex. The feature walk (`geometry::feature::build_loops`) reports each ring through such a vertex as `Open`, so the floor had no outer ring and the reader skipped it. The new `recognize::pinch` takes the walk's split rings as the outer ring and its holes, but only when it can prove them:
   - each ring is simple, and each span of each ring is a boundary edge of the face;
   - each hole has a vertex off the outer ring, and those vertices are inside the largest ring;
   - the largest ring's area less the hole areas is the face's facet area (relative slack 1e-3).

   Any other knotted face stays refused, as before. The geometry walk does not change, so no `FaceId` moves.
2. **A hole through the slot floor.** `slot_of` refused each floor with an inner ring. Now it refuses a floor with a boss only: an inner ring with a facet above the floor on one of its edges (`walls::Mesh::rises_from`). A hole has its wall below the floor, so the floor still reads as a slot. `islands` still counts every inner ring.

The decision record is `docs/decisions/2440-slot-floor-holes.md`.

## Readings

The issue's part was rebuilt in SolidCraft (plate 100 x 60 x 10, slot x 35..45 with its floor at z 7, four 6 mm through holes at (±42, ±22)) and exported as STL. It was then read through `camcraft-cli mcp`.

- Before: `{"count": 0, "features": []}`.
- After: one `slot`, floor z 7, top z 10, `islands` 2, width 10, length 60, ends `["open", "open"]`, centreline x 40 from y 30 to y −30.
- `detect_pockets {create: 0}` makes `Slot1`. With the stock fitted to the part, `generate` is ok, `verify` has no finding, and `post` writes 34 lines.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/mcp_pockets.rs`)

- `a_slot_with_a_hole_tangent_to_its_wall_is_still_a_slot`: a hand-built, watertight block whose diamond hole touches the slot wall at one vertex. The test checks the slot, its ends, its width, its length and its floor area (400 − 18). It also checks that `create` makes a Slot that generates.
- `a_slot_with_holes_through_its_floor_is_still_a_slot`: a height field with two holes in the floor (no tangency).
- `a_boss_standing_in_the_channel_is_not_a_slot`: the same field with bosses. It is still an open pocket, as before.

The first two fail on `upstream/main` and pass with this change. The boss test passes on both, so it guards against a fix that counts every inner ring as a hole.

## Gates

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 5 steps, 0 failed (`app suites: mcp_pockets`, `app suites: pocket_recognition` and the build steps).
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-app -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: the diff reaches 74 app heavy steps. They are not run yet. I will add the result in a comment before the PR is flagged ready.

## Not exercised

- A knotted face whose split fails the proof. It stays refused by code reading only; no test builds such a face.
- The UI Pockets page. It reads the same `recognize::pockets_of`, so it lists the same slots.

Changelog: `detect_pockets` now lists a slot whose floor has holes through it, also when a hole is tangent to the slot wall (#2440).

Fixes #2440

title: fix(drilling): Auto reads the depth in material; add the Deep cycle choice
body:
## What changed

1. **Auto reads the depth in material.** Auto chose the drill cycle by `R plane - bottom`, so the air above a hole's mouth counted as depth. A 3.5 mm spot under a 5 mm gap posted `G73 ... Q18`, with a peck step longer than the hole. Auto now reads the depth from the top of the material over the hole, never from above the R plane:
   - an axial hole (`crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs`): from the higher of the mouth (`Hole::entry_z`) and the material over the drill disk. The app reads that material (the part, the raw stock, and the stock that the program ahead leaves) and passes it in as `CycleParams::material_top`. The program ahead is simulated only where the raw stock stands above a mouth;
   - a radial hole (`cross.rs`): from the raw stock surface over the mouth, clamped to `0..=r_d`;
   - the setup sheet (`crates/app/src/setup_sheet/operations.rs`) names the cycle that the generator chose (the current cache). Without a current cache it says `auto`.

   Thus uncut stock over a mouth counts as depth, and air does not. The plunge still starts at the R plane, and the R word does not change.
2. **A new cycle choice `Deep`.** In the project file and MCP it is `"deep"`. In the combo it is "Deep peck (full retract)". It gives the existing `CycleKind::Deep`, which every canned-cycle post writes as `G83`. It is appended at combo index 10 and digest byte 10, so older operations keep their indices and stamps. The cross-hole cycle maps it before its `unreachable!` arm.
3. **The cycle words are listed.** `list_operation_types` already lists them (#3449). The test now also asks for `deep`.

Docs: the Drill section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/2443-drill-auto-depth.md`.

**Effect on programs.** Under Auto, a hole whose R plane is high above its mouth can change from `G83` to `G73`, or from `G73` to `G81`. A program that does not use Auto, and a hole whose R plane is at its mouth, posts byte-identical.

4. **The radial peck budget reads the full travel** (review fix). Auto picks the cross-hole cycle by the depth in material, but the pecks run from the R standoff. The budget now reads `r_d - bottom`, so a far standoff (30000 mm, or 1e20) is refused as `peck plan unusable`. It is never looped over. The loop also refuses a peck that makes no progress.
5. **Old caches read Stale** (review fix). Auto's output changes and its parameter digest does not. By the #3704 rule, `GENERATOR_OUTPUT_VERSION` goes from 1 to 2. Every cache saved under version 1 reads Stale once, the post refuses it by name, and it clears on regenerate. As #3704 did:
   - the catalog caches are rebuilt (`cargo xtask catalog`);
   - `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj`, `first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` and `first-router-part.camproj` are saved again (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1`; only stamps and the project version move);
   - the pinned stamps of `deburr_cache_stamp` and `wire_stamp` are captured again.

6. **Uncut stock counts** (found by the quick gate after the review fixes). A depth from the mouth alone hid stock over the hole: a raw bar r20 over a part r10 hid 10 mm of steel, and Auto chose chip breaks where full retracts are needed. Item 1 now reads the material over the mouth. The issue's case (stock faced to the plate top) still reads 3.5 mm and posts `G81`.
7. **The Auto limits are inclusive within one micron** (second review fix, b069c4477). A depth exactly on a limit chose the cycle by float roundoff. The cylinder case of `drilling_cross_box` reads 16 mm on a 4 mm drill (4 x d), and a stock radius of `25.000000000000004` gave full retracts on one host and chip breaks on another. `auto_kind` now compares with `AUTO_TOL` (1e-6 mm). The axial cycle, the radial cycle and the drill page all use `auto_kind`, so the whole class is closed.
8. **The two app tests of the material reading joined the `drill_prior` suite** (second review fix, 44f83e433). They were a new top-level binary `drill_auto_material`. They are now `crates/app/tests/drill_prior/auto_material.rs` (#3187). This PR adds no new top-level test binary.

## Goldens moved

- `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc`: the four drill blocks of `Drill1` change from `G83 ... Q6.` to `G73 ... Q18.` (lines 487, 493, 499 and 505). X, Y, Z, R and F do not change. For example, line 487 is now `G73 X38. Y23. Z-2.803 R22. Q18. F115.`
- `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.camproj`: the `Drill1` cache holds the four new cycles (`peck`, step 18) in place of `deep` (step 6).
- `crates/app/tests/cross_chain_reference/mod.rs` (`THREE_STATION`, the cylinder reference of `drilling_cross_box`): recorded again. The three holes read 16 mm in material on a 4 mm drill, which is 4 x d, so Auto now chooses the chip-break peck (19 moves: a 12 mm peck, a 1 mm hop, then to the floor) in place of the full-retract chain of efd1f26 (43 moves). That chain read the depth from the R standoff. Hole positions, floors, feeds and the traverses do not change. `OFF_CENTER` does not change.
- All other catalog `.camproj` files and the three example projects above: only the stamps and the project file version (83 to 84, the writer on the merged `main`) move. No other `.nc` file changes. `cargo xtask catalog` rebuilds every case with the same program.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `drilling::tests_auto_depth`:
  - `auto_measures_a_spot_from_its_mouth_not_from_the_r_plane` (the issue's case: G81, not G73)
  - `auto_reads_a_lower_r_plane_as_the_start_of_the_depth`
  - `the_deep_choice_is_the_full_retract_cycle`
  - `a_cross_hole_reads_its_depth_from_the_mouth_and_takes_deep`
- `mcp` suite: `drill_deep::the_deep_cycle_word_posts_full_retract_pecks_and_rides_the_project_file` (Auto posts G73, `deep` posts G83 through Fanuc, and the word survives a save and an open). `op_type_fields::list_operation_types_names_the_optional_fields_and_enum_words` now asks for `deep`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `cycle_combo::the_deep_peck_reads_in_plain_english` and `every_cycle_has_one_label_and_picks_itself_back` (11 choices).
- `camcraft-motion` lib: `drilling::tests_auto_depth::a_far_radial_standoff_is_refused_by_the_peck_budget` (explicit Peck, Auto and Deep, at R 30000 and 1e20).
- `camcraft-app` lib: `operation::stamp::tests::a_drill_cache_saved_before_the_2443_bump_reads_stale_and_does_not_post` (the catalog first-part `Drill1` with a pre-bump stamp reads Stale, the post refuses it by name, and once generated again it posts `G73` and no `G83`).
- `example_catalog`: `catalog_2d_first_part::{rebuilds,regenerates}` with the rebuilt program.
- `camcraft-motion` lib: `drilling::tests_auto_depth::an_auto_limit_reads_the_same_under_roundoff` (depths a few ULP over and under 1 x d and 4 x d keep their cycle; 2 microns over is the next cycle; a radial stock radius of 25 plus or minus roundoff gives the same moves). Mutation proof: with `AUTO_TOL = 0.0` it is red (`4 x d under roundoff: 1.6000000000000014e1`, `Deep` instead of `Peck`); restored, it is green.
- `drill_prior` suite, submodule `auto_material`: `uncut_stock_over_the_mouth_is_depth` (7 mm of raw stock over the plate: Auto pecks) and `stock_the_program_ahead_cut_away_is_not_depth` (a Face ahead cuts to the plate top: Auto posts G81, and the setup sheet says `drill`).
- `camcraft-motion` lib: `drilling::tests_auto_depth::auto_counts_the_material_over_the_mouth` and `a_cross_hole_counts_the_raw_stock_over_its_mouth`.
- `drilling_cross_box::a_cylinder_stock_chain_matches_its_numeric_reference` pins the new `THREE_STATION` chain. On this host it stays green under `AUTO_TOL = 0.0`, because this host reads the depth at or under 16. The motion test above adds the roundoff itself, so it is the pin that is red on every host. `drilling_cross_stock` keeps its readings.

## Readings

Second review round (head 44f83e433, macOS arm64, takeover by mkinney agents):

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, base 68bac804c): 730 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 64.8 min. It includes `drilling_cross_box`, `drill_prior`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `golden_cl` and the motion lib.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): 6 steps (release build, `motion light: lib`, `adaptive_troch_island`, `adaptive_troch_neck`, `adaptive_troch_parallel`, `app light: pocket_pass_start`), 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 6.1 min.
- Heavy lanes: not run in this round. AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" (#3556) says that no PR gets the full heavy lanes, and this PR is `P7`. The author's heavy run on 4cbc56ee9 is below. This round changes only the Auto limit by one micron and one test reference.

First review round (author):

- Quick gate on the final head 4cbc56ee9 (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 372 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 63.7 min.
- An earlier quick gate on b2ca05b43 had 3 failures:
  - `drilling_cross_box::a_cylinder_stock_chain_matches_its_numeric_reference` and `drilling_cross_stock::a_box_stock_and_an_off_origin_spindle_stand_off_the_raw_stock_plus_the_rim`. The depth from the mouth alone hid the raw stock over a cross hole. Item 6 fixes this, and the two tests pass with their old readings.
  - `egui_app::setup_wcs_tests::the_combo_lists_the_setups_post_range_by_its_names`. Main fixed this test in #4329. The merge of `upstream/main` (4cbc56ee9) brings in that fix.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask catalog` on the final head: no file changes.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`) on 4cbc56ee9: 51 steps (1 build, 7 `motion`, 43 `app`), 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 43.2 min. The known fails #1950 and #2849 are red as expected.

## Screenshots

The Cycle combo on the Passes tab of a Drill operation. "Before" is the same build with the new entry taken out for that render only.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2443/cycle-combo-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/2443/cycle-combo-after.png) |

- A real machine.

Fixes #2443

title: feat(mcp): list_posts, select_post, preview_post and save_post_script
body:
## What changed

This PR adds four MCP post tools (`crates/app/src/mcp/post_tools.rs`):

- `list_posts` lists each built-in post and each `.cps` file in the user posts folder. Each row gives the machine kinds that the post serves, `description`, `program_units`, `extension` and the declared options. A file that does not load gives its `problem`. `selected` is the document's post.
- `select_post` runs `SelectPost` through the session History. It is one undo step. `null` selects the default built-in post.
- `preview_post` runs a script (`source` or `path`) on a built-in sample (Facing, Contour, Pocket, Drilling) or on the document stream. It writes no file. It returns `ok`, `program`, `lines`, `warnings` and `swallowed`. A failed script returns `ok: false` and `errors` with the 1-based `line` in the script. The Boa runtime limits stop a script that loops.
- `save_post_script` saves a plain file name in the user posts folder. The folder is `CAMCRAFT_POSTS`, else `<data dir>/camcraft/posts` (the same order as the user machines folder). The script must load and run before the save. An existing file is replaced only with `overwrite: true`. The write is atomic.

Other changes:

- In a live app session, `save_post_script` needs approval as a `FileWrite`, and `select_post` as a `LimitEdit` (`mcp::live::requires_approval`).
- A hidden test hook `Server::set_user_posts_dir` (an `Env` field) points the folder at a temp folder.
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` is generated again (128 tools). `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` has the four rows. `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` has a "Post scripts" section.
- The decision file is `docs/decisions/2074-mcp-post-tools.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `mcp` suite, `post_tools::*` (6 tests):

title: feat(laser): the Laser Profile operation
body:
Slice 2b of #4081: the **Laser Profile** operation in the app.

**Stacked on #4270 (slice 1) and #4273 (slice 2a).** The branches of those PRs are in a fork, so this PR targets `main` and its diff includes them. The new work is the two commits after the merge commit `2a3670d48`: `a4cc1cf1f` and `ae360094b`. Merge #4270 and #4273 first. After that, this branch takes `git merge origin/main` and its diff is only slice 2b.

## What changed

- **Registry**:
  - New `OpType::LaserProfile`: stored kind id 49 and digest tag 49, appended.
  - New `Section::Laser` and `Family::Laser`. The Laser family admits only a laser cutter, and a laser cutter admits only that family.
  - The ribbon shows the Laser section on a laser cutter only.
  - The family door refuses laser work elsewhere: "a Laser Profile operation is laser cutting work; ... - mount a laser cutter first".
- **Params**: `LaserOp` has the waterjet's stored shape, with `power` (percent of the source's maximum) in place of the abrasive delay. It reuses the waterjet's lead, side and tab types. The command door checks the power: more than 0, at most 100.
- **Project file**: `LaserDto` (`"laser_profile"`), additive.
- **Generation**: `operation/laser_op.rs` resolves the heights and the laser head's kerf, then calls `motion::laser::laser_profile` (slice 2a).
- **Machine check**: `machine::waterjet::check_xy_ops` holds the X/Y gantry checks once. These are the family, the tool kind, rotary moves, feed ceilings and strokes. The waterjet and the laser call it with their own words. The waterjet sentences do not change.
- **Safety refusals until the laser post exists (slice 3)**:
  - The verification report says "<op>: laser posting is unavailable: beam on/off records, power records and pierce dwell records are not implemented".
  - The stock sim says "<op>: laser stock removal is not judged: the stock sim has no laser model".
  - The lathe voice refuses the op with its own sentence.
- **Tools**: the starter catalog gets `LZ-KERF-020` (`laser_tool(0.2)`). The empty-rack refusal names it. `camcraft_app::laser_tools` re-exports the tools module.
- **UI**:
  - New `laser_page.rs`: kerf, compensation, direction, open-run side and arcs on Geometry; the three heights; tabs; leads; and on Feeds the cut feed, **Power**, and pierce time. A power out of range is named on the page.
  - New original glyph `assets/ui/svg/op-laser-profile.svg`: an outlined head, a beam, sparks and the kerf gap. `cargo xtask icons` added only its PNG.
  - The waterjet page's `tab_fields` is shared.
- **MCP**: no new tool. `add_operation` and `edit_operation` reach the kind through the registry and the DTO. The `add_operation` description names the laser kind (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`).
- **Docs**:
  - New guide page `site/content/guide/operations/operations-laser.md`.
  - The operations index and `check-and-post/machines.md` name the laser.
  - Decision: `docs/decisions/4081-laser-op.md`.

## Screenshots

A laser cutter mounted, before (slice 1: no section) and after (the LASER group):

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4081/before-laser-ribbon.png)
![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4081/after-laser-ribbon.png)

The Laser Profile's Feeds tab (new page):

![feeds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4081/after-laser-feeds.png)

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/machine/laser_profile.rs` (the `machine` suite, 6 tests):
  - The family on a laser cutter only.
  - A holed plate: the hole first, every note in the laser's words, and the laser machine check clean.
  - The tool doors.
  - Create, edit, undo and redo, and the power door.
  - A byte-identical project round trip.
  - The post and sim refusals by name.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp/laser_profile.rs` (the `mcp` suite): add with tabs, edit the power, undo, redo, refuse 120 %, and generate.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/laser_ribbon.rs` (3): the ribbon on a laser cutter only and the dark cell with its tip on a mill; the own glyph and the leads tab; the Feeds tab with the power row and the named bad power.
- Updated:
  - `machine/laser_kind.rs`: a laser cutter now admits only the Laser Profile.
  - `tool_law::no_orphan_tool_kinds`: only the Laser Profile mounts a laser head.
  - `tool_gate::the_refusal_names_*`.
  - `ribbon::family_is_derived_not_forked` and `the_probe_appends_its_id_*`.
  - `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` (50 kinds).
  - `lathe_voice_tests` (37 refused kinds).
  - The catalog asset order (64).
  - The structural mill-tip test.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 626 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (81 min).
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- Heavy lanes: **not run** (owed before ready, as for #4273).
- No laser post: posting refuses laser work by name (slice 3).
- No shipped laser machine file and no machine-mode row: a user loads a `.mch` with `"kind": "laser"`.

Changelog: Operations: a Laser Profile operation (kerf offset, leads, tabs, power) for laser cutter machines; posting is not available yet.

title: feat(motion): Bore gets a Helical strategy (one helix to the floor, then a floor circle)
body:
## What changed

- New `BoreStrategy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_helix.rs`): `Rings` (the level ladder, the default and every earlier bore) or `Helical { spring_pass }`. `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` get the field `strategy`.
- A helical hole has these moves:
  1. A rapid over the helix start at the clearance height.
  2. A rapid down to the plunge height over the material.
  3. One continuous helix on the wall radius (`rc = R - r - leave`, the same circle as the last ring) to the floor.
  4. One flat floor circle. With `spring_pass`, a second floor circle.
  5. A feed to the centre at the floor, then a rapid up to clearance.
  
  A through hole's helix ends at the floor less the break-through. The helix is arcs of at most half a turn, so each arc posts as one G2/G3 with Z.
- The pitch is `stepdown`. The Heights tab calls it "Helix pitch" for a helical Bore. Climb is CCW, as for the rings.
- Two refusals in `BoreParams::validate`, before any move is built:
  - A hole that one helix cannot clear to the centre (`rc > floor reach`). For a flat end mill, the limit is twice the tool diameter. The message gives the core and the widest hole.
  - A helix steeper than 15 deg. The message gives the largest pitch that fits.
  - A helix inside the uncut core of a tool that is not centre-cutting (review finding on 4bd091166). The core is `plunge_law::CORE` of the tool radius. The wall circle must stand at least that far off the hole axis (`rc >= CORE * r`). The message names the helix radius, the uncut core and the smallest hole that the tool helixes (Ø9 for a Ø6 tool with no leave). A centre-cutting tool keeps the small helix.
- Pass starts at (#3360, from `main`) on a Helical Bore: one helix for each hole has no ring order. Inside and Outside are refused by name at the command (`sane.rs`) and in the generator (`bore_started`). The Passes tab shows the refusal under the row. Auto is unchanged.
- Bore `entry` (#3828, from `main` by #3832) on a Helical Bore: the helix is the entry of each hole. Plunge, the default, keeps the helix. Ramp and Helix are refused by name (`helical_entry_refusal`), at the command (`sane.rs`) and in the generator (`bore_started`). The project file and the stamp keep `entry` and `strategy` apart, so a reopened file shows the same refusal.
- Detect holes (`crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`) skips, and names, the holes that one helix cannot clear when the Bore is helical.
- Project file: `helical` and `spring_pass` on the `bore` record, written only when true. A ring ladder writes the same JSON as before. No version step (see the decision file).
- Stamp: the digest writes the strategy only for a helical Bore. A ring ladder keeps the stamp that it had.
- MCP: `list_operation_types` lists `helical` and `spring_pass` for `bore`. A params patch sets them.
- UI (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`): a Strategy combo and a Spring pass check on the Passes tab, the "Helix pitch" label on the Heights tab, and on the Lead-in tab main's Entry group, then a hint that the helix is the entry (hover text) and, for a Ramp or Helix entry, a refusal line. The group stays for the helix, so the user can set the entry back to Plunge.
- Guide: a "Helical strategy" part in the Bore section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and two rows in `site/content/guide/reference/refusals.md`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2830-helical-bore.md`.
- Mechanical: each `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` literal in the tests gets `strategy: Default::default()` (the ring ladder).

## Readings

The issue's counterbore, posted with `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`. The model is a revolved block with a Ø11 x 7 recess at the origin (top Z0). The tool is EM-0600-4FL (Ø6 flat), with a 1 mm pitch, climb, clearance 10 and retract 5. A scratch test built the document with the commands, then called `posting::post_script`. It is not committed. The status is Ok and the post has no warning. The cutting part of the program:

```
G0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z2
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z0 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-2 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-2.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-3 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-3.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-4 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-4.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-5 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-5.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-6 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-6.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-7 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G1 X0 Y0 Z-7 F600
G0 X0 Y0 Z10
```

- The helix starts at the plunge height (Z2) and drops 0.5 mm in each half turn to Z-7. There is no straight plunge.
- The two flat arcs at Z-7 are the floor circle. The G1 goes off the wall to the centre before the retract.
- The same document with the Rings strategy also posts with no warning (95 lines; a G1 plunge at the centre for each of the 7 levels).
- The first `G0 X2.5 Y0` line comes before the `G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10` line: the post writes its approach first. The Rings program has the same pattern.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_helix` (motion, new):
  - `the_counterbore_is_one_helix_on_the_wall_then_a_floor_circle_and_never_a_plunge`: the issue's Ø11 x 7 counterbore with a Ø6 flat end mill at 1 mm per turn. No axial feed, no `Plunge` move, the arcs on `rc`, nine turns from 2 mm over the top to the floor, one floor circle, a feed to the centre, a retract.
  - `the_spring_pass_is_a_second_floor_circle`, `conventional_milling_turns_the_helix_clockwise`, `a_through_hole_helix_runs_on_by_the_break_through`.
  - `a_hole_one_helix_cannot_clear_is_refused_with_the_widest_it_can` (Ø12 passes, Ø14 is refused with "2.000 mm core" and "12.000 mm").
  - `a_helix_steeper_than_the_limit_is_refused_with_the_pitch_that_fits` (Ø6.5: 32.5 deg; the given pitch then passes).
  - `the_rings_strategy_is_the_default_and_keeps_its_centre_dive`.
  - `a_helix_inside_the_uncut_core_of_a_non_centre_cutting_tool_is_refused`: the review's case (Ø6.5, Ø6 tool, 0.4 mm per turn, helix radius 0.25 mm). The NC tool is refused with "1.500 mm uncut core" and "9.000 mm". Ø9 and the issue's Ø11 counterbore still helix with that tool.
  - `a_helical_bore_refuses_a_pass_order_by_name`.
  - `a_helical_bore_refuses_a_ramp_or_helix_entry_by_name`: Ramp and Helix are refused with "Helical strategy" and the entry name; Plunge keeps the helix.
- `bore_helical` (app, new):
  - `the_issue_counterbore_is_one_helix_and_never_plunges_into_the_block`: through `operation::generate`, with a centre-cutting and a non-centre-cutting tool. `first_solid_plunge` finds no plunge, the verifier gives no warning, 18 half-turn arcs, the floor reached. The ring ladder still dives.
  - `a_hole_too_wide_for_one_helix_is_refused_through_the_operation`.
  - `a_small_helix_inside_the_uncut_core_is_refused_through_the_operation`: the review's probe through `operation::generate`. The NC tool is refused; the CC tool keeps the small helix with no plunge.
  - `a_helical_bore_with_a_pass_order_is_refused_by_name`: the command and the generator both refuse it.
  - `a_helical_bore_with_a_ramp_or_helix_entry_is_refused_by_name`: the command and the generator refuse Ramp and Helix; the pair survives the project file; Plunge is not refused; the pass-order refusal is still reached (one Bore arm in `sane.rs`).
  - `the_strategy_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_reads_rings`.
  - `the_stamp_moves_when_the_strategy_changes`.
- `operation::bore_reach::tests::detect_for_a_helical_bore_skips_the_holes_one_helix_cannot_clear` (app lib).
- `egui_app::tests::bore_strategy` (ui lib, new): the Strategy row defaults to Rings, Helical shows the Spring pass check, and the Heights tab names the pitch. `a_helical_bore_keeps_the_entry_group_and_says_the_entry_refusal`: a Ramp entry on the helix shows the refusal line and keeps the Entry combo; Plunge clears the line.
- `egui_app::tests::pass_start::a_helical_bore_says_the_pass_start_refusal` (ui lib): Rings take the order; Helical shows the refusal line.

## Gates

**Final head 68f223037** (takeover by mkinney, maintainer approval on #2830). It merges `upstream/main` at 1cf7390dc into cceaa2c52. The merge has no conflicts and no hand edits (class SAME). No rebase, no force-push.

Readings on 68f223037, against `upstream/main` 1cf7390dc:
- `cargo check --tests` for `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: builds. (Only `app` depends on `motion`.)
